signals.topic: Java SDK structured output treats all Java class fields as required, ignoring nullability annotations, causing LLM hallucination
signals.summary: When using `outputConfig(Class<?>)` with Java classes/records, all fields are unconditionally added to the JSON Schema `required` array. Annotations like `@Nullable`, `@JsonProperty(required=false)`, and `Optional<T>` types are all ignored. This forces the LLM to hallucinate placeholder values for fields the user intended to be optional.
aliases: Java nullability annotations ignored in schema generation
structured output required field false positives
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point: the core structured output feature is fundamentally broken for Java users because the schema generator cannot distinguish optional from required fields. The LLM produces hallucinated placeholder values instead of proper optional data, directly degrading output quality and breaking the intended use case of structured output. While count=1 prevents a P0 rating, the impact is significant — a primary SDK feature produces incorrect outputs — and the user explicitly offers a PR fix, indicating the issue is actionable and well-understood.

source_issues.title: [Java SDK] Structured Output: Java fields are always included in the required array, ignoring nullability markers
source_issues.evidence: The user's Java record with `@Nullable String` and `Optional<Integer>` fields still has all fields placed in the JSON Schema `required` array, causing the LLM to hallucinate string 'null', empty strings, or dashes to satisfy schema constraints. Multiple attempted workarounds (@Nullable, @JsonProperty, Optional) all fail.

signals.topic: Streaming aggregator fails to propagate container and tool result fields, causing 400 errors in multi-turn tool loops
signals.summary: The streaming mode aggregator in lib/streaming/_messages.py does not merge delta.container from message_delta SSE events, and the BetaContentBlock union in streaming mode is missing BetaToolSearchToolResultBlock and BetaWebFetchToolResultBlock types, causing them to be silently dropped. Both issues cause the subsequent API request to fail with 400 BadRequestError because required container_id or tool results are missing.
aliases: streaming accumulator drops tool result blocks
signals.review_reason: These are user pain points because they cause 400 BadRequestError on the second turn of multi-turn tool loops (issue #1424), and silently drop critical tool result blocks from streaming output (issues #1422 and #1421). The workarounds (manual SSE parsing or falling back to non-streaming) are unacceptable for production use. The affected tools (code_execution_20260120, tool_search, web_search) are core functionality.

source_issues.title: `get_final_message()` does not propagate `message_delta.container` into aggregated Message (breaks code_execution continuation)
source_issues.evidence: stream.get_final_message().container is None in streaming mode vs correctly populated in non-streaming mode. Subsequent API call fails with 'container_id is required when there are pending tool uses generated by code execution'. Reproduction code provided. Root cause confirmed in accumulate_event() missing container propagation.

source_issues.title: ParsedBetaContentBlock union missing tool_search/web_fetch result blocks — stream accumulator drops them from get_final_message()
source_issues.evidence: BetaToolSearchToolResultBlock and BetaWebFetchToolResultBlock absent from ParsedBetaContentBlock union. Raw SSE events carry the blocks but stream.get_final_message().content silently drops them. Discriminated union resolution fails and pydantic silently coerces or drops the blocks.

source_issues.title: BetaInputJsonEvent not fired for server_tool_use blocks during streaming
source_issues.evidence: BetaInputJsonEvent is fired for tool_use and mcp_tool_use but not server_tool_use, even though TRACKS_TOOL_INPUT correctly includes BetaServerToolUseBlock. Consumers cannot observe streamed input to server-side tools without raw SSE parsing.

signals.topic: Batch API intermittent 404 errors crash application and block batch operations
signals.summary: When calling batches.create(), batches.retrieve(), or batches.results(), the SDK intermittently returns 404 NotFoundError. The error is caused by server-side propagation delays, and in Case 2 it crashes the application because results() internally calls retrieve() which fails. All three operations are affected.
signals.review_reason: This is a P0 because it directly crashes user applications (traceback in Case 2 with full stack trace) and blocks the core Batch API workflow for three distinct operations. The issue has 3 separate failure modes within the same session, is reproducible within a 15-minute window, and has no reliable client-side fix — users must implement catch-and-fall-back logic.

source_issues.title: Intermittent `NotFoundError (404)` on Batch API
source_issues.evidence: Application crashes with traceback when batches.results() internally calls retrieve() and gets 404. Three distinct failure cases within 15 minutes affecting create(), retrieve(), and results() operations. Workaround requires catch-and-fall-back logic to messages.create().

signals.topic: Managed Agents MCP client supports only SSE transport, breaking integration with Streamable HTTP-only servers like Apify
signals.summary: The Managed Agents API connects to MCP servers using SSE transport exclusively. Apify deprecated their SSE endpoint on April 1, 2026 and now only supports Streamable HTTP, causing all Managed Agents sessions using Apify MCP to fail at initialization with 'SSE data line is not valid JSON'. There is no workaround.
signals.review_reason: This is a user pain point because it renders a major external MCP server (Apify) completely unusable with Managed Agents with no workaround, effectively breaking a key integration. The deprecation was on April 1, 2026 — an active, real-world breaking change affecting production deployments.

source_issues.title: Managed Agents MCP client only supports SSE transport — incompatible with servers that have dropped SSE (e.g. Apify)
source_issues.evidence: Apify deprecated SSE endpoint on April 1, 2026. MCP server 'apify' initialize fails with 'SSE data line is not valid JSON' (HTTP 405). Agent falls back to other tools and never uses Apify. No client-side workaround exists. Affected: all Managed Agents users with Apify MCP server.

signals.topic: PathLike objects in tuple form for file upload cause TypeError due to unreachable code path
signals.summary: Passing a PathLike object as the second element of a tuple to client.beta.files.upload (e.g. file=('foo.txt', Path('foo.txt'), 'text/plain')) fails because the tuple handler in _transform_file catches the tuple first, preventing the PathLike handler from being reached.
signals.review_reason: This is a user pain point because it causes a TypeError at runtime when users pass PathLike objects in tuple form (a natural and documented usage pattern per type hints). The code path is clearly dead due to tuple handler precedence over PathLike handler. Count=1 so P2.

source_issues.title: [BUG] `client.beta.files.upload` `PathLike` error
source_issues.evidence: Bug in _files.py _transform_file: tuple handler catches tuple first so PathLike handler is unreachable for tuples containing PathLike. Code references show the bug path: _transform_file line 49-74 catches tuple at first if block, making PathLike branch unreachable for tuple inputs. Documented with specific file and line references.

signals.topic: Outdated error message for long non-streaming requests links to non-existent documentation
signals.summary: Requesting large token counts without streaming raises ValueError referencing a documentation heading that no longer exists, leaving users without actionable guidance on how to handle long non-streaming requests.
aliases: streaming is required error docs outdated
signals.review_reason: This is a user pain point because users hitting the non-streaming token limit receive an error message pointing to a dead link, leaving them with no actionable guidance. The error blocks the request and the only path forward is brittle manual calculation. Count=1 so P2.

source_issues.title: API 'Streaming is required' error message is outdated
source_issues.evidence: ValueError references https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python#long-requests which no longer exists after commit 0e409217. No alternative guidance provided. User must reverse-engineer the safe token limit using _calculate_nonstreaming_timeout which is brittle.

signals.topic: bwrap sandbox breaks DNS resolution for localhost in Docker container environments, forcing users to disable sandbox entirely
signals.summary: When the SDK runs inside Docker containers with an outbound proxy (standard in AWS Bedrock AgentCore runtimes), the bwrap sandbox creates an isolated filesystem/network namespace without bind-mounting /etc/hosts from the host. This causes all localhost-based DNS resolution to fail (e.g., proxy at localhost:3128), making every AWS boto3 call fail with socket.gaierror. Users must set sandbox.enabled=false to restore pre-2.1.92 behavior, sacrificing sandbox security benefits.
aliases: localhost DNS broken in container sandbox
signals.review_reason: User pain point: sandbox feature is broken in a common deployment environment (Docker container with proxy), forcing a complete security trade-off. AWS API calls fail (blocking workflow), user has identified exact CLI version regression (2.1.81->2.1.92), and workaround requires disabling the sandbox entirely. Count=1 but impact is severe enough to qualify as P1.

source_issues.title: bwrap sandbox does not mount /etc/hosts — breaks localhost DNS resolution in containers
source_issues.evidence: Users must disable sandbox entirely (sandbox.enabled=false) as workaround, sacrificing security. All AWS boto3 calls fail with socket.gaierror inside sandboxed containers with proxy. Reproduction path clearly documented.

signals.topic: SDK generates invalid tool_use.id format during session resume, causing API 400 errors and blocking session resume
signals.summary: The SDK generates tool_use.id values in the format functions.{ToolName}:{N} (e.g., functions.AskUserQuestion:1) which contain '.' and ':' characters. These violate the API validation pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$. During session resume, these historical messages are replayed verbatim, causing API 400 errors. The session resume mainflow is completely broken.
signals.review_reason: User pain point: session resume — a core SDK feature — is completely blocked by invalid ID format. API returns 400 errors. Evidence includes exact API error message, specific invalid ID examples (functions.AskUserQuestion:1/2/4/5), and contrast with valid IDs from the same session. Count=1 but the failure is in a primary feature path with no known workaround.

source_issues.title: Invalid tool_use.id format during session resume causes API 400 error
source_issues.evidence: Mainflow failure: session resume is entirely blocked — API returns 400 with exact validation error: 'messages.7.content.1.tool_use.id: String should match pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$'. Reproducible with specific tool names. Valid IDs (call_*) coexist in same session from different code paths, proving the bug is in the tool_use.id generation.

signals.topic: ProcessError exit_code and stderr are stripped during error propagation, making subprocess failure diagnosis impossible
signals.summary: Three compounding defects: (1) ProcessError.stderr is a hardcoded literal 'Check stderr output for details' instead of actual subprocess stderr; (2) the original ProcessError is reduced to str(e) in the message reader; (3) it is re-raised as a bare Exception. Users cannot catch ProcessError, cannot access exit_code, and cannot get actual stderr output. Concurrent setups and CI pipelines are particularly impacted — no way to associate stderr with a specific failed query call.
aliases: ProcessError stripped of exit_code and stderr
generic Exception re-raised instead of ProcessError
signals.review_reason: User pain point: subprocess failure is a common occurrence in agentic workflows, and the SDK actively destroys all diagnostic information during error propagation. Users cannot programmatically handle subprocess failures (try/except ProcessError doesn't work), cannot get exit codes, and see only a hardcoded placeholder string for stderr. Three related issues (#515, #282, #238) confirm this is a recurring pattern. Count=1 but every subprocess failure is a blocking diagnostic failure.

source_issues.title: ProcessError exit_code/stderr stripped during error propagation; users see generic Exception with hard-coded 'Check stderr output for details' placeholder
source_issues.evidence: Verified reproduction shows: caught type is bare 'Exception', not 'ProcessError'; .exit_code and .stderr attributes do not exist on the caught exception. Original ProcessError with structured exit_code and stderr is destroyed across three files. Author cites three related closed issues (#515, #282, #238) as evidence this is a recurring pain point. CI and concurrent setups particularly impacted — no programmatic way to associate stderr with specific failed call.

signals.topic: Stop hook JS callback never fires — callback infrastructure bypassed when no shell-command hook registered
signals.summary: When a Stop hook is registered as a pure JS callback without a shell-command hook, the callback never fires. The CLI never sends a `hook_callback` control request with subtype `Stop`, so the callback infrastructure never reaches the user's function at all. Users must implement workarounds that bypass the Stop hook abstraction entirely.
aliases: Stop hook fast-path bypasses JS callbacks
signals.review_reason: This is a P1 because the Stop hook abstraction silently does nothing — no error, no warning, no log — forcing users to implement their own loop-level workarounds. The callback never fires at all, which is a complete functional failure of the hook mechanism, not just degraded behavior. Observed across 5+ production cycles with confirmed root cause in CLI not dispatching Stop events.

source_issues.title: Stop hook callback never invoked in v0.2.117 when only JS callback is registered
source_issues.evidence: Callback never fires across 5+ independent end_turn cycles in production. CLI side never dispatches `hook_callback` control request with subtype `Stop`. `handleHookCallbacks` exists but is never called. Workaround requires abandoning the Stop hook abstraction entirely.

signals.topic: Hardcoded 60s HTTP timeout on MCP POST requests not configurable — blocks long-running MCP operations
signals.summary: MCP POST requests (non-GET) have a hardcoded 60-second timeout in the bundled CLI that cannot be overridden by users. Long-running MCP operations fail with 'The operation timed out' with no user-accessible configuration.
signals.review_reason: This is a P1 because a hardcoded timeout with no configuration option directly blocks legitimate long-running MCP operations. Users cannot complete non-trivial MCP workflows. The timeout is not surfaced in SDK options, forcing users to hit a hard wall with no escape.

source_issues.title: Hardcoded 60s HTTP timeout on MCP POST requests does not seem to be configurable
source_issues.evidence: Hardcoded 60000ms timeout in bundled CLI binary for non-GET MCP requests. No user-accessible option to override. Users with legitimate long-running MCP operations have no workaround.

signals.topic: Linux CLI auto-discovery prefers musl over glibc binary — spawn fails with misleading ENOENT error
signals.summary: On Linux, SDK auto-discovery iterates the musl optional dependency before the glibc one. When both are installed (common with pnpm), the musl binary is picked even though it cannot execute on glibc-based systems. The spawn fails with a misleading 'Claude Code native binary not found' error that does not reflect the actual dynamic-loader incompatibility.
aliases: musl binary picked over glibc on Linux
wrong Linux binary selected by auto-discovery
signals.review_reason: This is a P1 because SDK initialization completely fails on the majority of Linux systems (glibc-based) when both optional deps are installed, with a misleading error message. Users lose hours debugging a 'binary not found' error when the file exists. No automatic recovery or informative error. The workaround requires manual binary path specification, which is not discoverable.

source_issues.title: Linux: musl binary preferred over glibc in v0.2.116 CLI auto-discovery
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced on Ubuntu 24.04 with pnpm installing both optional deps. Musl binary exists and is readable but fails to execute with 'required file not found' (missing glibc loader). Error message says 'binary not found' when file is present. Workaround requires manually specifying pathToClaudeCodeExecutable.

signals.topic: Background task_notification events buffered until next send() — model responds to stale combined state
signals.summary: When a background Bash task completes while the application is idle (not inside a for-await loop), the task_notification is buffered in the SDK and only delivered when the next send() triggers a drain. The model then sees the notification plus the new user message as back-to-back turns, confusing its responses.
signals.review_reason: This is a P1 because background task completion events are not delivered in real time, causing the model to respond to a combined state that includes a stale notification. This leads to confusing model behavior in any application that has idle periods between turns — which is the standard long-lived session pattern. No public API exists to manually drain pending events.

source_issues.title: Background `task_notification` events are lazy-drained: buffered until next send()
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed: task_notification delivered only on next send() call. Model responds to both buffered notification and new message together, causing confused/inconsistent responses. Reproduced with plain Bash + run_in_background: true, no custom MCP servers involved.

signals.topic: Bundled CLI uses undici with broken IPv6 happy-eyeballs fallback — Vertex AI OAuth hangs on dual-stack networks
signals.summary: The bundled CLI uses undici as its HTTP client for OAuth token refresh. On networks where Tailscale or similar provides an IPv6 ULA address but IPv6 is not routable to Google, undici's autoSelectFamily fails to fall back to IPv4, causing OAuth to hang indefinitely. Node's native https module handles this correctly.
aliases: Vertex AI OAuth hangs dual-stack network
signals.review_reason: This is a P1 because OAuth token refresh hangs indefinitely on any dual-stack network where IPv6 is present but non-routable (common with Tailscale, VPNs), completely blocking Vertex AI users from using the SDK. All chat operations fail with an empty error. No standard workaround exists; the bundled undici version has a known happy-eyeballs defect.

source_issues.title: Bundled cli.js fails IPv6 happy-eyeballs fallback — Vertex AI OAuth hangs on dual-stack networks
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed: undici fetch fails with ETIMEDOUT on dual-stack network where IPv6 ULA present but not routable to Google. Node native https module returns OK: 400 on same network. No standard workaround works (NODE_OPTIONS dns-result-order, /etc/hosts, macOS firewall). All chat messages fail for Vertex AI users on affected networks.

signals.topic: Bun 1.3.6 'directory mismatch' internal warning on every action run
signals.summary: Pinned Bun 1.3.6 has a known file descriptor tracking bug that emits 'Internal error: directory mismatch' warnings on every action run. Upstream fix exists. This is a cosmetic warning that does not affect functionality but creates noise in CI logs and may cause confusion or false positives in log monitoring.
signals.review_reason: 低频/边缘项：warning 本身不阻断功能（#1246 明确说 'You don't need to do anything'），但 #1234 提到 'blocks green CI for repos requiring all checks to pass'，说明对有严格 CI 要求的用户造成阻断。2 个 issue 均指向同一个 root cause（Bun 1.3.6 fd tracking bug），合并为 count=2。标记 P2: 低频边缘改进，非核心功能受损。

source_issues.title: Bun: Internal error 'directory mismatch for directory' in v1 action on GitHub-hosted runners
source_issues.evidence: Reproduces on every PR review in the reporting repo. Blocks green CI for repos requiring all checks to pass.

source_issues.title: Bun 1.3.6 emits 'Internal error: directory mismatch' warnings during action runs
source_issues.evidence: Every run logs the warning twice. Upstream Bun fix exists. Closed quickly (same day).

signals.topic: claude-sonnet-4-6 silently loops with empty turns for ~20 minutes producing no artifacts (exit status success)
signals.summary: Sonnet 4.6 model enters a tight loop of empty turns (stop_reason: null, output_tokens: 8) at ~2-3/sec for ~20 minutes, then exits as 'success' with zero artifacts. Workflows cannot distinguish this failure mode from clean completion. Control run on opus-4-7 completes successfully on identical inputs. Burns Claude Max weekly budget on zero-value runs.
aliases: model produces no output action succeeds
signals.review_reason: 主流程静默失败：action 以 'success' 退出但零产物产出，workflow 无法区分正常完成与失败。持续约 20 分钟的空转循环消耗 API 配额但无用户价值，在 Claude Max 计费场景下直接造成成本损失。已有 3 次可复现运行记录，opus-4-7 对照实验证明问题 Sonnet 特异性。符合 P0: 主流程阻断 + 可见日志证据 + 资源浪费。

source_issues.title: claude-sonnet-4-6 silent-fails with repeated empty turns (stop_reason: null, output_tokens: 8) — reproduces on v1.0.100 and v1.0.101
source_issues.evidence: 3 reproducible runs (v1.0.100 & v1.0.101) on same repo, same prompt, same scaffold. Action conclusion is 'success' despite no artifacts. Same workflow with opus-4-7 completes in 12 min with 2 commits pushed. ~20-min empty-retry loop burns API quota with no value. Direct cost impact on Claude Max weekly budget.

signals.topic: v1.0.100 breaks self-hosted/CI runners where claude.ai is unreachable (install.sh silent failure, bundled SDK binary not used)
signals.summary: v1.0.100 regression: install.sh curl fails silently behind corporate firewall, but action reports 'Claude Code installed successfully'. Then SDK throws 'Claude Code native binary not found' because pathToClaudeCodeExecutable points to non-existent file instead of falling back to bundled npm binary. Downgrade to v1.0.99 restores functionality.
aliases: bundled SDK binary not used v1.0.100 regression
signals.review_reason: v1.0.100 主流程阻断：action 报告安装成功但实际二进制不存在，SDK 立即崩溃，action 完全不可用。自托管 runner + 企业防火墙是真实部署场景，降级到 v1.0.99 的 workaround 证明根因定位清晰。虽然 count=1，但 evidence 充分（降级 workaround、回归定位到 PR #1235），符合 P0: 主流程阻断 + 可验证 workaround。

source_issues.title: v1.0.100 breaks environments where claude.ai is unreachable (install.sh silently fails, SDK bundled binary bypassed)
source_issues.evidence: Self-hosted runners behind corporate firewall (claude.ai unreachable, npm registry mirror available). install.sh curl SSL error silently swallowed. v1.0.99 with bundled binary works; v1.0.100 with pathToClaudeCodeExecutable set to non-existent path fails. Workaround: pin to v1.0.99. Regression introduced in PR #1235.

signals.topic: GitHub Actions workflow fails when actions/checkout uses persist-credentials: false (zizmor security recommendation blocked)
signals.summary: When actions/checkout uses persist-credentials: false (recommended by zizmor's artipacked audit to prevent GITHUB_TOKEN leaks), claude-code-action fails at setupBranch with 'could not read Username for https://github.com' because it runs git fetch before configuring its own auth. Blocks users from following security hardening best practices.
signals.review_reason: 安全加固阻断：用户被迫在安全最佳实践（zizmor artipacked 建议使用 persist-credentials:false）与 action 可用性之间二选一。setupBranch 在配置 git auth 之前执行 git fetch，导致企业安全合规场景下 action 完全不可用。auth 函数本身已存在，修复路径清晰但未调用。

source_issues.title: claude-code-action fails when actions/checkout uses persist-credentials: false
source_issues.evidence: Explicit reproduction with persist-credentials: false on checkout v6. Error in setupBranch before any user code runs. Auth setup in configureGitAuth() exists but is not called before git fetch in setupBranch. Blocks zizmor's artipacked security recommendation (GITHUB_TOKEN leak mitigation).

signals.topic: Bundled MCP servers (github_comment, github_inline_comment) silently fail to spawn on pull_request events — mcp_servers array always empty
signals.summary: On pull_request events, bundled MCP servers github_comment and github_inline_comment never spawn. The action correctly builds --mcp-config JSON and passes it via extraArgs, but the Claude CLI subprocess receives mcp_servers: [] in its init message. track_progress sticky comment never updates. No error is logged — silent failure.
aliases: mcp-config flag dropped in extraArgs forwarding
signals.review_reason: 关键功能静默失效：track_progress（action 的核心差异化功能）在 pull_request 事件下完全失效，sticky comment 永不更新。10+ 次可复现，日志证据完整（allowedTools 包含工具名但 mcp_servers 为空）。MCP 是 action 核心集成点，静默失效比报错更危险，用户无法感知问题。

source_issues.title: Bundled MCP servers silently fail to spawn on pull_request events (mcp_servers empty despite correct config build)
source_issues.evidence: 10+ reproducible iterations. SDK options.allowedTools contains mcp__github_comment__update_claude_comment, but CLI init reports mcp_servers: []. Claude repeatedly attempts the advertised tool and gets 'No such tool available'. Workaround: custom wrapper script instead of bundled MCP. Root cause suspected in extraArgs forwarding chain from query() to spawned CLI subprocess.

signals.topic: Extra usage credits inaccessible despite available balance — users blocked by rate limits and keychain errors
signals.summary: Users with positive credit balances cannot access extra usage credits. Both affected users on macOS (version 2.1.117) experience repeated 429 rate limit errors, SecKeychainSearchCopyNext failures, and inability to use the product after credit exhaustion. This is not a cost-of-usage issue — credits exist but are unreachable due to a product-side error.
signals.review_reason: Two separate users on identical platform/version (macOS, v2.1.117) report the same symptom: credits exist but are inaccessible, with identical error traces (keychain failures, 429s, request aborts). This is not a cost-of-usage complaint — it is a product-side error that blocks all further usage regardless of balance. High confidence, P1 for clear billing system failure.

source_issues.title: Difficulty accessing extra usage
source_issues.evidence: User added $5 credit to unlock extra usage; it consumed the $5 plus ~$2 more then reported out-of-extra-usage despite existing balance. Subsequent errors include: 'SecKeychainSearchCopyNext: The specified item could not be found in the keychain', 429 rate_limit_error, ECONNREFUSED, timeout, and Request aborted errors. Product completely unusable.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Extra usage credits not accessible despite available balance
source_issues.evidence: User had $34 of extra usage balance but cannot access it. Identical error patterns to #52140: SecKeychainSearchCopyNext failures, 429 rate_limit_error errors, repeated request aborts. Two separate users on same platform/version experiencing same symptoms.

signals.topic: Cowork fails to start on Windows — VM cannot boot or reach Claude API
signals.summary: Claude Code Cowork mode fails to start on Windows due to two distinct root causes: (1) on Snapdragon ARM64, the VM guest agent never starts after boot (daemon log 0 bytes, HCS errors); (2) on x86 Windows, the Hyper-V Default Switch is configured as Internal type with no external uplink, making the VM unable to reach api.anthropic.com. Both scenarios completely block the Cowork product.
aliases: Cowork VM network unreachable on Windows
signals.review_reason: Two separate Windows Cowork failures both completely block the Cowork product (a major Claude Code feature) on Windows machines. Snapdragon ARM64 failure leaves the VM in a non-functional state; the network misconfiguration failure prevents API connectivity entirely. Both are reproducible, both have comprehensive diagnostics, both leave the user with zero Cowork functionality on Windows.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Cowork doesn't run on Snapdragon processor
source_issues.evidence: Snapdragon X X126100 (Qualcomm Oryon CPU), Windows 11 Pro ARM64, Claude 1.3883.0.0 arm64. VM connection timeout after 60 seconds. Daemon console log is 0 bytes — guest agent never starts after ARM64 boot. Multiple HCS/HCN warnings in log. Cowork completely non-functional.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Cowork fails - VM cannot reach Claude API, Default Switch is Internal type with no external uplink (Windows 11 Pro, v1.3883.0)
source_issues.evidence: Cowork consistently fails with 'Can't reach the Claude API from Claude's workspace.' Root cause: Hyper-V Default Switch is type Internal with no external adapter assigned — VM boots but cannot route to api.anthropic.com. Full network diagnostics provided showing TcpTestSucceeded on host but unreachable from VM.

signals.topic: Max (20x) weekly quota depletes disproportionately — Opus 4.7 1M context burns 50%+ of tier budget in 2-3 days
signals.summary: Users on the top-tier Max (20x) plan observe their weekly quota depleting at a rate far exceeding the '20x' positioning. After 2-3 days of normal single-session Opus 4.7 usage, the weekly bar shows 51% consumed with no itemized breakdown. A single short burst right after session reset immediately adds ~17% to the current-session bar. Community evidence links this to the Opus 4.7 / 1M-context rollout.
aliases: Max plan quota depletes too fast
signals.review_reason: Significant cost impact: top-tier users are paying for 20x budget but burning 50%+ in under half a week with no breakdown to self-manage. Issue explicitly links to 6 community reports describing the same pattern post-Opus 4.7/1M rollout. While count=1 in this dataset, the cross-referenced community signal and the billing severity warrant P1.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Max (20x) weekly limit depletes disproportionately — 51% mid-week, ~17% within minutes of session reset
source_issues.evidence: User on Max (20x) plan reports 51% weekly quota consumed after 2-3 days of normal single-session Opus 4.7 (1M context) work. Session already at ~17% immediately after reset. Issue explicitly cross-references 6 community reports (#50742, #47587, #51715, #51219, #41174) all describing the same root cause. User states: 'The weekly cap on Max (20x) should actually reflect the 20x positioning.' No itemized breakdown available to self-diagnose.

signals.topic: Inline image regression breaks session after message retract — session left in inconsistent state
signals.summary: Regressing a user message that contains an attached/pasted image leaves the Claude Code session in a broken state. Subsequent messages are not processed correctly; the session must be abandoned or forked to continue. No recovery path exists within the session.
aliases: Session breaks after retracting image message
signals.review_reason: Regression that breaks a core workflow (message retract/regress) with no in-session recovery path. The session becomes unusable and forces the user to abandon progress or fork. Clear user impact: loss of session continuity and forced restart of work. P1 despite count=1 due to complete workflow breakage.

source_issues.title: Session breaks after regressing a user message that contains an inline image
source_issues.evidence: Attempting to regress/retract a user message containing an attached image leaves the session in a broken state. Subsequent messages show error: 'Claude couldn't process that message. Try sending it again.' Resending does not recover. Long-running 1M-context session on Windows. User notes no recovery path short of forking or starting a new session.

signals.topic: VS Code extension session history shows empty — past sessions not resumable after window reload
signals.summary: The Claude Code VS Code extension's session history UI consistently shows no past conversations after VS Code window reload. The extension writes session data to .jsonl files under ~/.claude/projects/ but fails to write corresponding entries to ~/.claude/history.jsonl, which is the index the session history UI reads. Users lose the ability to resume past sessions entirely.
aliases: history.jsonl not updated by VS Code extension
signals.review_reason: Complete loss of session history persistence: 14 sessions written to disk but completely invisible to the UI. Every VS Code reload erases all session context for the user with no recovery path within the product. Has a reproducible root cause (history.jsonl not being written). Significant UX degradation for the VS Code extension.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Session history shows empty — extension writes session files but never updates history.jsonl
source_issues.evidence: 14 session .jsonl files written to disk (~90-114KB each) but history.jsonl stopped updating on 2026-04-01 (3+ weeks ago). history.jsonl shows 0 entries for the analytics-tests-status-report project. Current active session not in index. Extension log shows list_sessions_request fires with no response. All past session context lost on VS Code reload.

signals.topic: Skills notebook missing GitHub repo clone prerequisite
signals.summary: The skills introduction notebook instructs users to 'cd /path/to/claude-cookbooks/skills' without ever mentioning that they must first clone the GitHub repository. Users follow the instructions and hit a dead end, unable to locate the directory.
signals.review_reason: This is a documentation gap that blocks first-time users from completing the skills introduction tutorial. The user directly describes frustration from being unable to proceed. While low frequency (single issue), it is a clear onboarding/main flow blocker for the skills cookbook, which is a core entry point.

source_issues.title: [BUG] intro to skills should point at github repo as install prereq
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly reports following the cookbook instructions and getting stuck because the prerequisite of cloning the GitHub repo is never mentioned. Direct quote: 'try to follow the instructions without first having cloned a github repo which is never mentioned — be frustrated.' This is a first-time user onboarding blocker for the skills tutorial.

signals.topic: Managed agents webhook feature documented but not visible in Platform Console
signals.summary: The CMA_operate_in_production cookbook describes webhook registration under Settings → Webhooks in the Claude Platform Console, but users find no such setting exists, leaving the documented production pattern inaccessible.
signals.review_reason: The cookbook documents a webhook-based production pattern that users cannot actually use because the Console setting described in the docs appears to be missing or relocated. This creates a documentation-product mismatch that prevents users from implementing the production deployment pattern for managed agents. While labeled a 'question', the core issue is a documentation gap with real user impact.

source_issues.title: [QUESTION] Managed agents webhooks
source_issues.evidence: User tried to follow the managed agents production cookbook but found no webhook registration option in the Claude Platform Console despite the notebook explicitly describing it under Settings → Webhooks. The user is left without a clear path to implement the documented production pattern.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: orphaned bun server.ts processes survive termination and burn CPU/RAM indefinitely
signals.summary: Telegram plugin child processes survive SIGTERM and orphan-watchdog, each consuming 80–100% CPU and ~190MB RAM. After 10 days one user had 7 orphans; after 3 days another had 14 zombies totaling ~250 CPU-hours burned.
signals.review_reason: Significant resource leak causing clear cost losses and system degradation. Orphaned processes accumulate without bound, each burning a full CPU core and ~190MB RAM. Recurs every time Claude Code exits without graceful shutdown, making this a systemic failure for any user who restarts or interrupts a session.

source_issues.title: telegram plugin: orphaned bun server.ts procs survive SIGTERM and orphan-watchdog on macOS
source_issues.evidence: Orphaned bun server.ts processes survive SIGTERM and burn 90% CPU and ~190MB RAM each. After ~10 days, 7 orphaned processes were running, totaling ~1.3GB RAM and 7 CPU cores consumed. Orphan-watchdog mechanism fails to clean them up.

source_issues.title: [telegram] Server leaks and pegs 100% CPU when Claude Code exits without SIGTERM-ing plugin
source_issues.evidence: Each surviving bun server.ts spins at 80–100% CPU indefinitely. Accumulated 14 zombie processes over 3 days, totaling ~250 CPU-hours burned. Clear cost loss through sustained resource consumption.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: inbound messages from Telegram never appear in Claude Code session despite bot receiving them
signals.summary: The Telegram plugin's MCP bridge silently drops inbound messages. Bot polls correctly, receives messages (confirmed via JSON-RPC stdout), MCP server shows connected, but Claude Code UI never renders the messages — no channel tag appears. Core plugin functionality entirely broken despite correct installation and pairing.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking — the primary use case of receiving user messages via Telegram is entirely non-functional. Bot and MCP server appear healthy, giving users no indication of where the breakage lies. Confirmed reproducible with clean install and multiple DM policy attempts.

source_issues.title: Claude Code 2.1.117 Telegram plugin issue
source_issues.evidence: Inbound messages from Telegram never appear in Claude Code session. Bot polls correctly, receives messages (confirmed via JSON-RPC notifications on stdout), MCP server shows connected, but Claude Code UI never displays messages. No <channel source="telegram"> tag appears. Dock icon bounces indicating activity but nothing renders. Core plugin functionality completely broken despite correct setup.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: child Claude Code sessions (agents, skills, subprocesses) kill the parent session's bot poller via PID contention
signals.summary: When Claude Code spawns a child session (agents, skills, subprocesses), the child starts its own Telegram MCP server and sends SIGTERM to kill the parent's poller before taking over, disconnecting Telegram tools from the parent session mid-conversation.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking — any use of agents, skills, or subprocesses while using the Telegram channel immediately disconnects the Telegram MCP tools from the parent session. This makes it impossible to combine Telegram with Claude Code's core feature set, rendering the channel integration effectively unusable for active development.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin: child sessions kill parent's bot poller (PID contention)
source_issues.evidence: When Claude Code spawns a child session (agents, skills, subprocesses), the child starts its own Telegram MCP server, detects the parent's poller is alive, and sends SIGTERM to kill it before taking over. This disconnects Telegram MCP tools from parent session mid-conversation. Users cannot use Telegram alongside any other Claude Code functionality.

signals.topic: M365 Connector: access blocked by organization policy despite full admin consent and no Conditional Access policies
signals.summary: M365 MCP connector fails on both Claude.ai and Claude Code returning 'Your organization's access policy blocks the MCP server' despite Global Admin consent granted, no Conditional Access policies, and other Microsoft integrations working fine. Request is rejected by Anthropic backend before reaching tenant.
signals.review_reason: Key functionality unavailable — M365 Connector is entirely non-functional for enterprise users who have correctly configured admin consent. The error message is actively misleading (blames tenant policies), and sign-in logs confirm the rejection occurs at Anthropic's backend. This is a complete block for the primary enterprise integration use case.

source_issues.title: [BUG] M365 Connector - Your organization's access policy blocks the MCP server despite admin consent granted
source_issues.evidence: M365 MCP connector fails on both Claude.ai and Claude Code returning 'Your organization's access policy blocks the MCP server' despite Global Admin consent granted, no Conditional Access policies blocking, and other Microsoft integrations working fine. Sign-in logs show no failed auth attempt — request rejected by Anthropic backend before reaching tenant. Misleading error message blames tenant configuration.

signals.topic: Ralph-loop: cross-session state leak causes unrelated Claude Code sessions in the same directory to receive loop prompts and be blocked
signals.summary: When CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is unset, ralph-loop's state file gets an empty session_id causing the guard to short-circuit and match every session. Unrelated sessions sharing the project directory have their Stop hook intercepted and receive the loop prompt, breaking their workflow.
aliases: ralph-loop stop hook affects other sessions
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking — when ralph-loop is active in any session, all unrelated Claude Code sessions in the same directory have their Stop hook intercepted, breaking their normal workflow. This makes the loop feature dangerous to use in collaborative or multi-session development environments.

source_issues.title: ralph-loop: cross-session state leak when CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is unset at setup
source_issues.evidence: Ralph-loop leaks into other Claude Code sessions sharing project cwd. The Stop hook in every unrelated session gets blocked and receives the loop prompt. Iteration counter advances by whichever session happens to Stop first. Root cause: when CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID env var is unset, state file gets empty session_id, causing guard to short-circuit and match every session.

signals.topic: docx skill: TableOfContents renders empty in Google Docs, hyperlinks non-functional
signals.summary: The docx skill's TableOfContents generates .docx files without `cachedEntries`, causing empty TOC placeholders in Google Docs after upload/conversion. Clicking 'refresh' produces entries whose hyperlinks do not resolve. Root cause is docx-js's `<w:sdt>` cache not being populated, and Google Docs relying on that cached content rather than running TOC field update on open.
aliases: TOC renders blank Google Docs conversion
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed functional bug with clear root cause: docx-js only emits populated `<w:sdt>` cache when `cachedEntries` is provided, but the docx skill's SKILL.md does not document this requirement. Users whose workflow involves Google Docs (a common real-world path) get a broken TableOfContents — a core document feature. The bug is reproducible (works in Word, fails in Google Docs), blocks the intended use of the TOC feature, and the fix requires explicit documentation of a non-obvious API option.

source_issues.title: [Bug] docx skill: TableOfContents renders empty in Google Docs without cachedEntries
source_issues.evidence: User reports that calling `new TableOfContents(...)` without `cachedEntries` causes TOC to render as empty placeholder in Google Docs after .docx upload. Hyperlinks in refreshed TOC entries do not resolve. Works correctly in Word but fails in Google Docs workflow.

signals.topic: skill-creator exhausts Pro subscription limits without delivering usable results
signals.summary: Pro subscription users report that the skill-creator consumes subscription quota (5 hours × 2 = 10 hours of usage time) without producing any usable code or skill output. The tool becomes completely unusable mid-session, preventing users from completing skill creation tasks and wasting their paid quota.
aliases: skill-creator no useful output consumed limits
signals.review_reason: This is a quota/rate limit pain point with clear financial impact. A paying Pro subscriber reports that the skill-creator consumed their subscription's time quota (5h × 2 = 10h) without producing any usable output. This is a case of quota being consumed with zero benefit — a form of cost loss for the paying customer. The blocking nature (cannot code, cannot set up context) makes it a non-trivial experience degradation.

source_issues.title: skill-creator eliminated the whole limits (5 hours x 2 times) without any result
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states: 'With a Pro subscription, it's impossible not only to code something, but even to set up a context via skills, agents, and memory.' and 'The skills-creator is unusable after your new limits!' and 'Very disappointed...' — direct report of quota being consumed without delivering usable output.

signals.topic: Idle session failures — goosed backend terminates or SSE stream breaks after inactivity
signals.summary: Sessions in open idle windows fail after 5–30 minutes of inactivity; all sessions in sidebar fail simultaneously as goosed process is killed by macOS disk-write limits or SSE stream breaks.
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports of the same phenomenon: sessions fail after being left idle. This is a main flow blocker — users cannot leave sessions open and return to them. Root cause spans SSE stream breakage and macOS disk-write coalition kills (see issue 8711).

source_issues.title: [BUG] SSE stream breaks on idle open windows — all sidebar sessions fail simultaneously
source_issues.evidence: Sessions in open idle windows show errors after 5–30 minutes of inactivity. All sessions fail simultaneously because they route through the same goosed backend. SSE event stream between Electron renderer and goosed has broken.

source_issues.title: Chat window breaks when continuing after hour(s)
source_issues.evidence: Starting a chat, leaving it for hours, then returning and pressing send causes the chat window to break — typed message is gone, chat inaccessible, new chat won't open. Workaround requires closing and reopening goose window.

signals.topic: ACP provider streaming renders discrete message bubbles instead of coalesced text
signals.summary: All ACP providers yield each streaming text chunk as a fresh Message without an id, causing the Desktop UI to render hundreds of discrete bubbles instead of a single coalesced streaming message.
aliases: ACP provider chat renders multiple bubbles
streaming text chunks not coalescing in Desktop
signals.review_reason: Affects every ACP provider user on Desktop — the streaming UX is fundamentally broken, rendering the chat interface unusable with all ACP connections. Clear root cause identified in acp/provider.rs.

source_issues.title: ACP providers: streaming text chunks render as separate Desktop message bubbles
source_issues.evidence: All ACP providers (claude-acp, amp-acp, codex-acp, copilot-acp, pi-acp) yield each streaming text chunk as a fresh Message without an id, causing the Desktop UI to render hundreds of discrete timestamped bubbles instead of a single coalesced streaming message. Root cause: Message::assistant() creates messages with id: None every call, so the frontend's coalescing check never matches.

signals.topic: Goose CLI fails to launch — process suspended with tty output error after commit b7aea3dc9
signals.summary: Goose CLI process immediately suspends with 'zsh: suspended (tty output)' on every invocation. Breaking commit identified as b7aea3dc9 where spawn_blocking spawns 'bash -l -i' inheriting terminal control.
signals.review_reason: Complete CLI launch failure introduced by a recent commit — every user pulling the latest main branch cannot run goose from the terminal. This is a main flow blocker, though count=1 and single repo prevent P0.

source_issues.title: Goose CLI Will Not Launch
source_issues.evidence: Goose CLI process immediately suspends with 'zsh: suspended (tty output)' on every invocation from terminal. Breaking commit identified as b7aea3dc9. The spawn_blocking call to resolve_login_shell_path spawns 'bash -l -i' which inherits terminal control, causing suspension. Complete CLI launch failure.

signals.topic: Desktop electron app builds with empty screen from source via 'just run-ui'
signals.summary: Building the desktop electron app from source using 'just run-ui' results in an empty screen, blocking contributors from working on the desktop UI.
aliases: desktop app from source not working
signals.review_reason: Blocks all developers from running the desktop app from source, completely preventing contribution to the Desktop UI. Main flow for development is broken. Not P0 because count=1 and single repo.

source_issues.title: [BUG] 'just run-ui' build the electron app with empty screen
source_issues.evidence: Building the desktop electron app from source using 'just run-ui' results in an empty screen. User followed CONTRIBUTING.md exactly. The app built in debug mode should work the same as the release build but does not. Screenshot provided showing empty screen.

signals.topic: Slash commands from config file not working with broken tab completion on Linux
signals.summary: Slash commands appended in the configuration file cannot be used on Linux CLI and tab completion does not work.
signals.review_reason: Slash commands and tab completion are core UX features that are broken on Linux, preventing users from efficiently invoking configured commands. Report is brief but clear about both features being non-functional.

source_issues.title: slash commands bug
source_issues.evidence: Slash commands appended in the configuration file cannot be used on Linux CLI. Tab completion also does not work. User provided screenshot showing configured slash commands are not recognized by the system.

signals.topic: Browser startup timeout on low-end machines blocks initialization
signals.summary: 用户在使用低性能机器时，Stagehand 在 5000ms 内无法完成浏览器启动，导致 TimeoutError: waitForFirstTopLevelPage，主流程直接阻断。当前 timeout 不可配置，用户无解。
aliases: Browser startup timeout on low-performance machines
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1 不满足高频标准，但该问题属于主流程阻断（init 阶段崩溃），且用户明确指出 timeout 不可配置，缺乏变通方案，具备明确的用户影响证据。count=1 且单仓，按规则默认不 P0，但 P1 合理。

source_issues.title: TimeoutError: waitForFirstTopLevelPage (no top-level Page) timed out after 5000ms
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告在低性能机器上，浏览器启动耗时超过默认 5000ms 超时，直接抛出 TimeoutError: waitForFirstTopLevelPage，主流程阻断，且当前无 timeout 配置接口，用户无法自行延长。

signals.topic: Cloudflare 防护站点无法自动化，浏览器卡在 about:blank 并触发内部错误

Internal errors when interacting with Cloudflare challenges

source_issues.title: Stagehand Issue: Unable to Automate Cloudflare-blocked sites (Blank Browser, and Internal Errors)
source_issues.evidence: 用户在目标站点（Jiji.ng，Cloudflare 防护）上报告：浏览器窗口卡在 about:blank 不导航；stagehand.page 无法解决 Cloudflare 人机验证；调用 observe/act 时抛出内部错误 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading replace)' 和 'StagehandError: Invalid argument: you may have called act with an empty ObserveResult'。主流程完全阻断，关键功能不可用。

signals.topic: Mounts映射目录后权限拒绝，文件读写主流程阻断

signals.review_reason: count=2，有两位不同用户报告同一根因（mounts 配置导致 LocalSandboxProvider 权限错误），直接阻断文件读写这一核心操作，且 issue 2423 仍为 open 状态。

source_issues.title: 使用mounts映射目录后，deer-flow提示无权限读取该目录下的文件
source_issues.evidence: 用户配置 mounts 将 /opt/my-workspace 映射到 /mnt/project 后，代理读取文件时收到 permission denied 错误，直接阻断文件读取主流程。

source_issues.title: 映射目录后deer-flow无权限读取目录的文件

signals.topic: ask_clarification 工具调用后对话历史丢失，代理状态断裂

aliases: 对话历史丢失 after clarification
signals.review_reason: count=2（issues 2425 和 2442），同一根因被中英文用户分别报告。问题直接破坏多轮对话的上下文连贯性，使代理在 ask_clarification 后丧失历史记忆，属于主流程阻断。

source_issues.title: 智能体调用ask_clarification工具后，丢失了之前的对话历史
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告使用 make_lead_agent 后，调用 ask_clarification 并收到用户回复时，HTTP 请求中丢失了之前的对话历史，导致代理认为用户响应是一个全新会话，上下文完全断裂。

source_issues.title: Lead agent: conversation history missing in LLM request after ask_clarification follow-up
source_issues.evidence: 同一问题的英文版报告，指出可能是 checkpoint/thread 绑定问题、状态合并问题或客户端/gateway 请求结构问题，已关闭但根因未明确修复。

signals.topic: _apply_prompt_caching 超出 API cache_control 4个断点限制，导致多轮对话 LLM 400 错误
signals.summary: _apply_prompt_caching() 在每个 system prompt 文本块、最后 N 条消息的内容块和最后一个工具定义中均注入 cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"}，在多轮对话中超出 Anthropic API 和 AWS Bedrock 的 4 个断点限制，引发 400 Bad Request 错误，导致代理无法正常响应。
signals.review_reason: issue 2448 提供了清晰的技术分析：cache_control 注入超出 API 限制导致 400 错误，直接阻断多轮对话中 LLM 的调用能力。虽然 count=1，但影响明确属于主流程阻断，置信度高。

source_issues.title: _apply_prompt_caching exceeds the 4 cache_control breakpoint limit in multi-turn conversations
source_issues.evidence: _apply_prompt_caching() 在 system prompt、消息内容块和工具定义中均注入 cache_control，超出 Anthropic API 和 AWS Bedrock 的 4 断点限制，在多轮对话中引发 400 Bad Request，直接阻断 LLM 调用。

signals.review_reason: issue 2438 描述了 Docker sandbox 文件创建失败的用户可复现场景，直接阻断代理的文件生成核心能力。虽然 count=1，但提供了明确的错误信息和使用场景，属于主流程阻断，keep=true。

source_issues.title: 使用docker sandbox创建文件任务失败
source_issues.evidence: 用户使用 docker sandbox 配置 volumes 挂载 ./project:/app/project 后，代理使用 /app/project 目录创建文件时失败，报错 'Docker sandbox environment has a problem, cannot access filesystem'，阻断文件生成这一核心任务。

signals.topic: 创建新技能始终失败：LLM request 400 错误

signals.review_reason: issue 2422 描述了技能创建关键功能的反复失败（always fails），前端报错明确但后端无日志，指向隐性的 prompt/请求体问题，属于关键功能不可用。count=1，但体验影响为'完全不可用'，review_reason 提供强证据支撑 P1。

source_issues.title: 创建新技能总是失败：LLM request failed: Error code: 400
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告创建新技能时总是失败，前端显示 'LLM request failed: Error code: 400' 错误，后端日志无异常记录，关键功能（创建技能）完全不可用。

signals.topic: API provider request failures causing session termination (various providers)
signals.summary: Multiple API providers (vLLM Qwen3.6, AWS Bedrock) fail with unrecoverable errors (UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT, stream ends without output) that exhaust the consecutive mistake counter and permanently stop the task session. Users have no recovery path within the same task.
signals.review_reason: Both issues represent persistent, unrecoverable API failures that completely block the main task workflow. #10359 affects every vLLM Qwen3.6 task; #10330 affects every Bedrock task. Both exhaust the consecutive mistake counter with no user recovery path, meeting the '反复失败+关键功能不可用' threshold.

source_issues.title: Qwen3.6 leading to 'UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT'
source_issues.evidence: vLLM Qwen3.6 causes UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT on every task. Not recoverable — retry countdown is interrupted by model thinking, loops forever. Session never completes.

source_issues.title: Model stream repeatedly ends without producing output when using AWS Bedrock — hits consecutive mistake limit
source_issues.evidence: AWS Bedrock causes 'stream ended without producing output' on every task. After 6 consecutive failures the session stops entirely. Persistent, blocks all Bedrock usage.

signals.topic: Vertex AI global region returns 404 for Claude models — incorrect hostname construction
signals.summary: When Vertex AI region is set to 'global' for Claude models, Cline constructs the endpoint URL with an incorrect hostname (global-aiplatform.googleapis.com) that doesn't exist, resulting in 404 errors. The correct global endpoint uses aiplatform.googleapis.com without a region prefix.
aliases: Vertex AI Claude global routing failure
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm the same root cause: Vertex AI global region is completely broken for all Claude models due to incorrect hostname construction. The 'global' region is offered by Cline's own UI (supportsGlobalEndpoint: true) but is non-functional, misleading users.

source_issues.title: Vertex AI: Global endpoint for Claude models returns 404 - incorrect hostname construction
source_issues.evidence: Global-aiplatform.googleapis.com returns 404. Correct URL is aiplatform.googleapis.com (no region prefix). Root cause: AnthropicVertex SDK constructs hostname from region parameter directly, producing invalid 'global-' prefix.

source_issues.title: vertexAI multi region
source_issues.evidence: Global location for Claude Opus 4.7 returns 404 Not Found or ECONNRESET. Same model works with specific region.

signals.topic: YOLO mode consecutiveMistakeCount counter not resetting on user-message boundary causes premature task termination
signals.summary: The consecutiveMistakeCount in YOLO mode persists across user-message boundaries. When a user types 'continue', the counter from the previous (failed) turn carries over, causing the very first tool call of the resumed session to trip the limit and end the task — even before the model makes any mistakes in the new turn. Affects power users who rely on 'continue' to recover from transient infrastructure hiccups.
aliases: YOLO mode mistake counter carries over
signals.review_reason: Strong user evidence from empirical data (149 trips analyzed). This is a UX design flaw: the counter should reset at user-message boundaries but does not, causing premature task termination on every 'continue' action. Power users who rely on task resumption after transient failures are systematically blocked.

source_issues.title: consecutiveMistakeCount should reset on user message boundary (YOLO trips on 'continue' / task resumption)

signals.topic: Checkpointer fork produces duplicate messages in branched state
signals.summary: Forking a checkpoint with checkpointer=True causes duplicate human messages in new branch; related regression prevents second regenerate from creating new branch
signals.review_reason: Both issues are main flow blockers for LangGraph's core time-travel/branching feature. Issue 7593 causes state corruption (duplicate messages in forked branches). Issue 7592 is a confirmed regression silently losing branch history. Together they leave no working configuration for checkpoint-based branching on recent versions, breaking a flagship capability.

source_issues.title: Agent with checkpointer=True: forking human message produces duplicate human messages in new branch
source_issues.evidence: Forking with checkpoint_id produces branch containing both original and forked human message instead of only the new one. Workaround unavailable on 1.1.7+: checkpointer=False hits separate #7592 regression, leaving no fully working configuration.

source_issues.title: Regression in 1.1.7 (#7498): Second regenerate from latest checkpoint doesn't create new branch
source_issues.evidence: Calling astream twice with same parent checkpoint_id (regenerate) fails to create second sibling branch on 1.1.7+. AI output silently overwrites branch 2 instead of creating branch 3. Bisected to PR #7498.

signals.topic: BinaryOperatorAggregate silently drops values arriving after Overwrite in concurrent supersteps
signals.summary: In concurrent supersteps, regular values arriving after an Overwrite are silently discarded with no error or warning
signals.review_reason: Two independent reporters confirm the same silent data loss bug in concurrent supersteps. Regular values arriving after Overwrite are completely discarded with no error or warning. This can corrupt application state in production concurrent workloads without any indication something went wrong. Both count and evidence clearly meet P1 threshold.

source_issues.title: bug: BinaryOperatorAggregate.update() silently drops values arriving after Overwrite
source_issues.evidence: In concurrent supersteps, task write ordering can cause regular values arriving after Overwrite to be silently discarded. No error, no warning. Reproduction shows expected=15, actual=10 when Overwrite(10) precedes value 5.

source_issues.title: BinaryOperatorAggregate silently drops regular values that appear after an Overwrite
source_issues.evidence: When updates=[5, Overwrite(10), 3], final value is 10 instead of raising InvalidUpdateError. The '3' is completely, silently lost. User calls it 'dangerous' because silent data loss during state transition can corrupt application state.

signals.topic: ToolNode._arun_one blocks event loop when using sync wrap_tool_call
signals.summary: ToolNode falls back to calling sync wrap_tool_call on event loop thread, stalling concurrent tool execution
aliases: sync tool call event loop stall
signals.review_reason: This blocks LangGraph's concurrent multi-tool execution model. When a sync wrap_tool_call lacks an async variant, the event loop stalls and all concurrent tool executions are serialized. This defeats the purpose of concurrent tool dispatch and causes severe performance degradation for multi-tool agent workflows.

source_issues.title: bug: ToolNode._arun_one blocks event loop when using sync wrap_tool_call
source_issues.evidence: ToolNode._arun_one falls back to calling sync wrap_tool_call directly on event loop thread. Since _afunc dispatches via asyncio.gather, a single blocking sync wrapper serializes every concurrent tool execution and stalls the event loop.

signals.topic: SyncPregelLoop.put_writes caches INTERRUPT/ERROR writes bypassing retry logic
signals.summary: Sync path is missing the INTERRUPT/ERROR guard present in async path, causing failed writes to be cached and replayed as successes
signals.review_reason: This silently hides failures from retry logic. When a task fails and CachePolicy is enabled, the error write is cached and replayed as a valid result on subsequent invocations. Task failures appear to succeed, corrupting workflow state without any indication of the original failure.

source_issues.title: bug: SyncPregelLoop.put_writes caches INTERRUPT/ERROR writes (async path already guarded)
source_issues.evidence: SyncPregelLoop.put_writes persists task writes unconditionally. AsyncPregelLoop.put_writes already has guard for INTERRUPT/ERROR, but sync path is missing it. With CachePolicy enabled, failed/interrupted task error writes are cached and replayed on next invocation, bypassing retry logic.

source_issues.evidence: schemas.py line 3 imports typing_extensions but it's not declared in package dependencies. Clean environments like GitHub Actions runners fail with ModuleNotFoundError when running langgraph CLI commands.

No chat completions succeed.

signals.topic: Semantic conflict resolution is missing in v2 ADD-only pipeline, causing duplicate memories and degraded search quality
signals.summary: When contradictory facts are added sequentially (e.g., 'my name is Alice' then 'my name is Bob'), both are stored as separate ADD events instead of producing an UPDATE. The documentation claims 'Latest truth wins when contradictions detected' but the implementation only does MD5 hash deduplication with no semantic conflict detection. Results in duplicate memories, wrong get_all() counts, and degraded search quality.
signals.review_reason: Core memory deduplication is broken — the documented contract ('Latest truth wins') is not implemented. This directly degrades the primary value proposition of Mem0 (memory management). Two independent user reports confirm the behavior mismatch.

source_issues.title: ADD-only architecture doesn't implement conflict resolution for semantically similar memories
source_issues.evidence: v2.0.0 ADD-only architecture only uses MD5 hash deduplication; semantic contradiction not detected. Contradictory facts stored as separate ADD events.

source_issues.title: fix: semantic conflict resolution missing in v2 ADD-only pipeline
source_issues.evidence: memory.add('my name is Alice') then memory.add('my name is Bob') both produce ADD events; get_all() returns 2 results instead of 1. Code-only change for main.py:784-803 needed.

signals.review_reason: First-touch experience for new users is broken. Official demo crashes immediately upon entering a message, which directly blocks adoption and onboarding. While only 1 issue, it represents a critical first-impression failure in the documented quickstart path.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Interactive memory demo app is broken

All LLM requests go to api.openai.com instead of the configured custom endpoint, causing 401 errors.
aliases: openai_base_url lost when using custom LLM endpoint

source_issues.title: OpenMemory: DB config overrides LLM_BASE_URL / EMBEDDER_BASE_URL env vars — openai_base_url lost for self-hosted users

signals.topic: Concurrent AsyncMemory writes corrupt Qdrant HNSW index causing IndexError crashes
signals.summary: When multiple coroutines call AsyncMemory.add()/update()/delete() concurrently (e.g., async agents processing events in parallel), Qdrant's HNSW index becomes corrupted producing IndexError: 'index N is out of bounds for axis 0 with size M'. Subsequent reads (search(), get()) either return wrong results or crash. Requires full index rebuild to recover.
aliases: Qdrant index corruption from concurrent writes
HNSW index out of bounds error
signals.review_reason: Async agents are a primary use case for Mem0. Concurrent writes (a natural pattern for async agents) silently corrupt the HNSW index with no recovery mechanism. This causes permanent data corruption requiring index rebuild, which is a significant operational incident.

source_issues.title: Bug: concurrent AsyncMemory writes corrupt Qdrant HNSW index ('index N is out of bounds')
source_issues.evidence: AsyncMemory write methods use asyncio.to_thread() running Qdrant upsert in parallel threads. Qdrant's HNSW graph builder is not re-entrant; concurrent writes corrupt the index causing IndexError on reads and writes. Full rebuild required to recover.

signals.topic: FoundryChatClient silently drops default_headers parameter — authentication/setup silently fails
signals.summary: When users pass default_headers to FoundryChatClient or FoundryAgent, the headers are silently ignored and never included in HTTP requests. This causes silent authentication failures where users believe configuration is wired up correctly when it is not.
signals.review_reason: API silently accepts a parameter (default_headers) but never uses it. User's auth/setup appears configured but HTTP requests lack required headers — causes silent auth failures with no error. Classic broken contract anti-pattern.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: FoundryChatClient(default_headers=...) and FoundryAgent(default_headers=...) silently drop custom headers
source_issues.evidence: default_headers parameter accepted but not forwarded to HTTP layer. Authentication/authorization headers silently disappear. User has no indication of failure.

signals.topic: background=True causes infinite tool-call loop — SDK re-reads same response instead of posting tool results
signals.summary: When background=True is combined with function tools, continuation_token leaks into mutable_options across tool-loop iterations. The SDK repeatedly GETs the same response_id instead of POSTing tool results, causing 40+ identical tool calls and an empty final response.
signals.review_reason: background=True with tools creates an infinite loop that consumes API quota with 40+ redundant calls and returns empty results. This is a cost-loss scenario (repeated API calls with no valid output) combined with a main-feature (tool use) being completely broken.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: `background=True` causes infinite tool-call loop, tool-result submissions inherit background mode
source_issues.evidence: Bug confirmed: continuation_token persists across tool iterations in mutable_options, causing SDK to re-retrieve the same response. 40+ identical tool calls observed. Empty final response text. Core tool-use loop is broken.

signals.topic: RoundRobinGroupChat raises raw Python exceptions instead of validation errors for invalid participants input
signals.summary: RoundRobinGroupChat does not validate the participants argument type before use, leaking raw AttributeError/TypeError to users when None, strings, integers, or non-agent objects are accidentally passed. Users receive confusing internal implementation errors instead of a clear validation message.
aliases: raw Python exceptions for invalid participants
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed UX/blocker issue. The issue provides reproducible steps showing that passing None, a string, or a list with a non-agent object to RoundRobinGroupChat produces raw Python internal exceptions (AttributeError, TypeError) instead of user-friendly validation messages. The reporter explicitly identifies these as 'realistic user mistakes' and provides exact reproduction code. This directly blocks users from diagnosing configuration errors, fitting the definition of 'experience significantly degraded'.

source_issues.title: RoundRobinGroupChat raises raw AttributeError/TypeError for invalid participants instead of a clear validation error
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with 3 cases: participants=None raises TypeError, participants='string' raises AttributeError, participants=[valid_agent, 'bad'] raises AttributeError. Body explicitly states: 'These are realistic user mistakes. It would be much easier to debug if AutoGen raised a clear TypeError or ValueError explaining that participants must be a non-empty list/sequence of ChatAgent instances.' Labels include 'needs-triage' indicating confirmed UX issue.

signals.topic: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing, risking full system compromise and credential theft
signals.summary: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor writes LLM-generated code to disk and executes it as a subprocess with full host privileges, with only a UserWarning (easily suppressed) as the sole safeguard. Production deployments following quickstart examples are vulnerable to arbitrary code execution, credential theft, and lateral movement.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed critical security vulnerability with direct user impact. The issue documents that LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor has no runtime security control — only a UserWarning that is easily suppressed in production environments. The attack scenario is concrete and reproducible: a user following official quickstart examples would deploy unsandboxed code execution vulnerable to indirect prompt injection. Impact includes full system compromise, credential theft (SSH keys, cloud tokens), and lateral movement. This fits 'key functionality with dangerous behavior' and 'obvious cost/critical impact'.

source_issues.title: [Security] LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing
source_issues.evidence: Severity: HIGH. The executor writes LLM-generated code to disk and executes it via asyncio.create_subprocess_exec with full host privileges. The only safeguard is a UserWarning at construction time that is easily suppressed in production (e.g., -W ignore, logging pipelines). Concrete attack scenario: a user following quickstart examples deploys the executor, the LLM receives indirect prompt injection, and malicious code (e.g., SSH key exfiltration via subprocess) is written to disk and executed. Impact includes full system compromise, credential theft (SSH keys, cloud credentials, API tokens), lateral movement, and data destruction. Confirmed by agent-audit security scanner.

signals.topic: WebKit/Linux: page.fill() does not fire React 19 onChange events, breaking form interaction tests
signals.summary: On WebKit/Linux, Playwright's page.fill() does not fire React 19's onChange handler on synthetic input events, causing controlled inputs to remain empty and submit buttons to stay disabled. Tests that pass on Chromium and Firefox fail exclusively on WebKit/Linux.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：page.fill() 是表单测试的核心 API，在 WebKit/Linux 上对 React 19 彻底失效（onChange 不触发），意味着基于 React 19 的应用在 WebKit/Linux 下无法进行任何表单自动化测试。这是明确的跨浏览器行为不一致，且 React 19 是当前主流框架版本，影响范围显著。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: WebKit/Linux] page.fill() does not fire React 19 onChange on synthetic input events
source_issues.evidence: page.fill() on React 19 controlled input fails on WebKit/Linux only; button stays disabled; same code passes on Chromium and Firefox on same Linux runner; also fails with page.type() and keyboard.type(); only workaround is page.evaluate() which bypasses React controlled state

signals.topic: Assertion retry intervals waste up to 1000ms of timeout budget by skipping final check before deadline
signals.summary: Playwright's retryWithProgressAndTimeouts uses escalating intervals [100, 250, 500, 1000ms]. When the deadline fires during the 1000ms sleep, the assertion aborts without a final check, causing legitimate elements that appeared before the deadline to be missed and tests to fail incorrectly.
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降 + 主流程假失败：断言是测试的核心组件，当 timeout 在 1851-2849ms 区间时会浪费最多 999ms 的 budget 并导致本应通过的断言错误失败（假阴性）。影响所有使用该 retry 机制的断言（toBeVisible、toContainText 等核心 API），是明确的测试可靠性问题。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Expect assertions with escalating retry intervals skip final check before deadline, wasting up to 1000ms of timeout budget
source_issues.evidence: Detailed repro with code: element appears at 1900ms with 2500ms timeout, but check at 1850ms misses it and deadline at 2500ms fires during 1000ms sleep; affects ALL locator assertions using retryWithProgressAndTimeouts: toBeVisible, toBeHidden, toContainText, toHaveText, etc.; up to 999ms of timeout budget wasted

signals.topic: v1.59 breaks CI due to version mismatch between installed Playwright package and Docker image
