signals.topic: Google Gemini parallel tool calls cause 400 Bad Request — Gemini rejects multiple separate function response messages
signals.summary: When Gemini 2.0-flash invokes multiple tools in parallel via GoogleAIGeminiChatCompletionService, the connector sends multiple separate 'function' role messages (one per tool response) instead of a single 'function' role message containing all responses in one parts array. Gemini rejects this with 'number of function response parts is equal to the number of function call parts' error. This blocks any workflow requiring parallel tool execution.
signals.review_reason: Parallel tool execution is a common and important agentic pattern. This bug silently terminates multi-tool workflows with a 400 API error, making any complex agent behavior using multiple parallel tools impossible with Gemini. Two independent reports (issues #12528 and #12554) confirm the pattern.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Gemini - 2 parallel plugin call exception: number of function response parts is equal to the number of function call parts
source_issues.evidence: Gemini API returns 400 with 'number of function response parts is equal to the number of function call parts'; request contains 2 separate 'role: function' messages instead of one with both responses in parts array; Gemini 2.0-flash with multiple registered tools

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Google Gemini unable to perform Multiple Function calls in single request
source_issues.evidence: Any request with multiple function calls to be performed ends the stream without exception; works with single function call; gemini-2.5-pro model; confirmed similar to issue #10597 in Python SDK

signals.topic: Python Redis connector vector search (FT.SEARCH) completely broken — AttributeError and KeyError on every search call
signals.summary: The Python Redis connector's vector search is completely broken on the committed dependency resolution. RedisHashsetCollection._inner_search passes a deprecated StorageType enum to redisvl's process_results(), causing AttributeError on all search calls; additionally the hashset deserializer unconditionally accesses missing vector fields causing KeyError when include_vectors=False (the default). The redisvl ~=0.4 pin resolves to 0.15.0 where the API changed at 0.5.0, and the pyproject.toml constraint prevents a clean upgrade path. No version satisfies both SK's redis>=6 and redisvl's old API.
signals.review_reason: Core feature (vector search) completely non-functional for all Python Redis users on committed dependencies. Blocking: no search works at all, no workaround available, no compatible redisvl version exists given dependency constraints.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Vector search (FT.SEARCH) via the Python Redis connector is broken
source_issues.evidence: AttributeError: 'StorageType' object has no attribute 'index' on every search call; KeyError: 'vector' in hashset deserializer when include_vectors=False; redisvl ~=0.4 resolves to 0.15.0 where API changed at 0.5.0

signals.topic: Python RedisJsonCollection.delete() silently fails when prefix_collection_name_to_key_names=True — records never deleted
signals.summary: RedisJsonCollection._inner_delete does not apply the collection-name prefix to keys before calling JSON.DEL, so with prefix_collection_name_to_key_names=True (the parent class default) the command targets non-existent keys, returns 0, and records are never deleted. No error is raised — the failure is completely silent. The sibling RedisHashsetCollection correctly calls _get_redis_key(), but the JSON path does not.
signals.review_reason: Data mutation silently fails with no error signal. Records persist in the database after delete calls return success, leading to data inconsistency and leaked storage in production. The failure is completely silent (0 return value from JSON.DEL is not treated as error), making it extremely hard to diagnose.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: RedisJsonCollection.delete() silently fails when prefix_collection_name_to_key_names is enabled
source_issues.evidence: Wire capture shows JSON.DEL targeting raw key 'test-1' instead of 'sk_cov_xxx:test-1'; record persists after delete call; no exception raised; affects any user with prefix_collection_name_to_key_names=True

signals.topic: Python Redis connector sends malformed FT.CREATE PREFIX — one character per prefix instead of collection name
signals.summary: The Redis connector passes a plain string to redis-py's IndexDefinition(prefix=...), which iterates the string character-by-character, creating one single-character prefix per character of the collection name. In single-collection setups the bug is silent (Redis Stack accepts the malformed command). In multi-collection deployments, collections with overlapping characters register overlapping prefixes and can match each other's keys.
signals.review_reason: Correctness defect in index creation. In single-collection mode the bug is masked but wastes Redis resources with spurious prefixes. In multi-collection deployments on shared Redis it causes cross-collection key collisions, leading to incorrect search results and data leakage between collections. Not P0 because the simple single-collection case works silently.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Redis connector sends malformed FT.CREATE PREFIX (one prefix per character of collection name)
source_issues.evidence: Wire capture shows 'PREFIX 27 r e d i s _ j s o n...' for collection 'redis_json_list_data_model'; in multi-collection deployments on shared Redis, indexes match unintended keys across collections

signals.topic: GoogleAIGeminiChatCompletion does not include tools/functions in API requests — plugin function calling completely broken
signals.summary: When using AddGoogleAIGeminiChatCompletion with FunctionChoiceBehavior or GeminiToolCallBehavior, the connector does not serialize the tools field into the API request to Gemini. Function calls are never generated even when plugins are correctly registered. The same configuration works correctly with AddOpenAIChatCompletion using Gemini's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, confirming the settings and plugin definitions are correct.
aliases: GoogleAI Gemini function calling not working
signals.review_reason: Core functionality (tool/function calling) is completely broken for GoogleAI Gemini users. Any agent relying on plugin execution via Gemini will fail to invoke functions. This is a high-impact integration defect affecting .NET users of the GoogleAI connector.

aliases: Usage limit shown despite Plus subscription
Pro account shows out of quota
You're out of Codex messages on Plus account

The combination of paying users being unable to access the service they purchased constitutes a high-impact P1 issue. The 'out of quota' error at 141k/258k context usage also suggests a possible context-window vs message-quota confusion, indicating a UX messaging problem at minimum.

signals.topic: Session state lost after system shutdown or restart — rollout not persisted, resume fails
signals.summary: Codex CLI sessions that reach usage limits or are interrupted by battery shutdown are not flushed to disk, making them unresumable after restart. Hours of work are lost with no recovery path.
aliases: Session not persisted after battery shutdown
codex resume fails after system shutdown
signals.review_reason: Session state loss after shutdown is a direct user-impacting data loss event. The user explicitly reports hours of work gone with no recovery path, which meets the 'high cost loss' bar for a P0 despite being count=1. The root cause (session never flushed to disk in resumable form) is a clear implementation bug, not a request or edge case.

source_issues.title: Session lost after battery shutdown + update — no rollout persisted for resumable session
source_issues.evidence: A long-running session that reached usage/query limit was lost after battery depletion shutdown. No rollout .jsonl file exists for that day. User explicitly states: 'Several hours of work lost with no recovery path.' Prior similar sessions worked correctly, indicating regression.

signals.topic: PATH shadowing by Codex.app bundled Node breaks native macOS addons (Next.js, SWC, Vitest)
signals.summary: Codex.app prepends its internal Resources directory to PATH, causing the bundled hardened-runtime Node to shadow the user's installed Node. This breaks npm packages with native .node addons, producing misleading code-signature errors.
aliases: Bundled Node shadows Homebrew Node on macOS
Native addons fail due to PATH collision
signals.review_reason: This is a systemic installation-side effect that silently breaks a developer's entire Node.js toolchain. The error manifests far from the cause (looks like codesigning issue), making it hard to diagnose. It affects all shell sessions on macOS post-installation and blocks common development workflows including Next.js, SWC, Vitest, and Lightning CSS. The root cause is the installer modifying global PATH rather than exposing only the codex CLI binary.

source_issues.title: Codex.app prepends bundled Resources directory to PATH, causing bundled Node to break native addons on macOS
source_issues.evidence: PATH is modified to prepend the entire Codex.app Resources directory. which node resolves to Codex's bundled Node instead of Homebrew Node. This causes ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED for common native addons (Next.js/SWC). The same addon loads fine with Homebrew Node. The failure is persistent and affects all shell sessions.

signals.topic: apply_patch tool hangs indefinitely under sandboxed workspace-write path on macOS/Linux
signals.summary: The apply_patch tool hangs with zero success/error output when run under workspace-write sandbox mode, 0/5 deterministic repros, but works immediately under danger-full-access. Blocks the core file-editing workflow.
aliases: apply_patch tool never returns under workspace-write
signals.review_reason: A core tool (apply_patch) hangs indefinitely with no error output under the normal sandboxed path, while working with the unsandboxed bypass. This completely blocks the intended workflow (applying patches to files) for any user relying on workspace-write mode, which is the default safe mode. The fact that it silently hangs rather than failing fast makes it particularly dangerous as it wastes user time and blocks CI/CD pipelines.

source_issues.title: macOS 0.122.0: apply_patch hangs under workspace-write but succeeds under danger-full-access
source_issues.evidence: 5/5 deterministic repros on a 2-line file under workspace-write mode all hung until killed. The same patch succeeds immediately under danger-full-access. No success, error, or timeout is produced — the tool just never returns. This is a regression from 0.120.0 where it returned a timeout error.

signals.topic: Context compaction fails on Azure Foundry deployments, blocking long conversations
signals.summary: On Azure Foundry deployments, context compaction fails 100% of the time with a 'high demand' error, preventing users from continuing conversations beyond the context window.
aliases: Remote compact task fails on Azure Foundry
signals.review_reason: The compaction failure is a conversation-blocking regression for Azure Foundry users. Long conversations cannot be continued at all — this is a main-flow failure for enterprise/self-deployed users. The 'high demand' error is misleading and suggests a backend availability issue or misrouted API call for Azure deployments. While count=1, the nature (100% failure rate on a specific deployment type) makes it likely to affect others.

source_issues.title: Compact fails in CLI and Codex VS Code Extension
source_issues.evidence: User on Azure Foundry deployment: 'When a chat gets to the compaction it fails 100% of the time and cannot be continued.' Error: 'Error running remote compact task: We're currently experiencing high demand.' Chat otherwise works. Compaction is essential for long conversations.

signals.topic: Windows sandbox path separator causes WorkspaceStartError and SkillsConfigError
signals.summary: Windows uses backslash (\) as path separator while Modal/Linux sandboxes use forward slash (/). When users on Windows pass Windows paths to Modal sandbox operations (workspace init or skill loading), the binary path resolution fails with ExecNonZeroError/WorkflowStartError or SkillsConfigError. Both issues share the same root cause: path separator incompatibility on Windows hosts when the local path is forwarded to a POSIX sandbox binary.
signals.review_reason: Two separate issues from the same user (onmyraedar) demonstrate a consistent Windows+Modal sandbox path separator incompatibility. Both block the sandbox main workflow on Windows: one prevents workspace initialization entirely (WorkspaceStartError), the other prevents skills from loading (SkillsConfigError). The root cause is identical. Count=2 meets the P0 threshold when backed by strong user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: `WorkspaceStartError` on Windows
source_issues.evidence: User on Windows running SandboxAgent with Modal client gets `ExecNonZeroError: no such file or directory` for `\tmp\openai-agents\bin\resolve-workspace-path-*` binary. Main workflow blocked: sandbox fails to start.

source_issues.title: Skill source directory unavailable on Windows
source_issues.evidence: User on Windows gets `SkillsConfigError: lazy skill source directory is unavailable` when using LocalDirLazySkillSource. Skills directory exists inside sandbox but path separator mismatch causes load failure. Main workflow blocked: skills cannot be loaded on Windows.

signals.topic: RealtimeAgent stuck when tools fire during active response stream
signals.summary: When a tool is registered to a RealtimeAgent and the tool fires while a response is already in progress, the SDK emits a 'create.response' event that conflicts with the active stream, raising a RealtimeError: 'Conversation already has an active response in progress'. The agent gets stuck and waits indefinitely for the customer to respond, blocking the main interaction flow.
aliases: Conversation already has an active response in progress
signals.review_reason: Real-time agent interaction is a core use case for the SDK. When tools fire during an active response, the agent enters an indefinite stuck state waiting for the customer. This is not a cosmetic issue — it blocks the main interaction loop and requires user intervention. The issue is open and confirmed against production usage (v0.14.2), with multiple triggering scenarios described (async concurrent tools, external create.response).

source_issues.title: Realtime Tools cause agent response to cut off
source_issues.evidence: User reports RealtimeError 'Conversation already has an active response in progress' when tools fire during an active stream. The agent gets stuck and waits for customer response. Triggered by async tool calls and 'create.response' events outside the agent. Confirmed in v0.14.2 production with edge cases still present in v0.13.1 improvement.

signals.topic: Windows import of agents.sandbox.sandboxes fails with ModuleNotFoundError: fcntl
signals.summary: The agents.sandbox.sandboxes package eagerly imports the Unix-only backend from unix_local.py, which depends on fcntl and termios. On Windows, importing this package immediately raises ModuleNotFoundError, preventing any sandbox usage on Windows platforms entirely.
signals.review_reason: A simple import statement crashes on Windows. This is a startup crash that makes the entire sandboxes package unusable on Windows — users cannot even begin to use the feature. Reproducible with a single-line import. Count=1 prevents P0 but the crash severity and complete platform blockage justify P1.

source_issues.title: Windows: import agents.sandbox.sandboxes fails with ModuleNotFoundError: fcntl
source_issues.evidence: Simple `import agents.sandbox.sandboxes` on Windows (Python 3.14.2, SDK 0.14.2) immediately raises ModuleNotFoundError. The Unix-only backend is imported eagerly, blocking any Windows user from using the sandboxes package at all.

signals.topic: stream_events() silently swallows background run-loop exceptions
signals.summary: When Runner.run_streamed() is used with a sandbox agent, any exception raised in the background run loop before the first stream event is silently swallowed. The result appears to finish cleanly (final_output=None, new_items=[], raw_responses=0) with no indication that a fatal error occurred. Users must dig into result.run_loop_task.exception() to find the real failure, creating a poor debugging experience.
signals.review_reason: Early failures are completely invisible to callers — the SDK returns a seemingly successful result with no errors while the actual exception is buried in an internal task object. This creates a deceptive debugging experience where users believe execution succeeded when it actually failed. Not P1 because it's not a workflow blocker (sandbox still runs) but it's a significant UX degradation for debugging.

source_issues.title: Surface run-loop exceptions in stream_events() for early failures
source_issues.evidence: Early exceptions in background run loop during run_streamed() are silently absorbed. Result appears clean (final_output=None, empty items) with no error signal. Users must manually inspect internal task state (run_loop_task.exception()) to discover the actual failure. Poor debugging UX, especially for new contributors.

signals.topic: Tool names with spaces silently transformed without warning
signals.summary: The transform_string_function_style function replaces spaces with underscores before comparing to decide whether to emit a warning. Tool names containing spaces are silently lowercased and space-replaced without triggering the warning, making it hard to debug mismatched tool names downstream.
aliases: space in tool name silently handled
signals.review_reason: A logic bug in name transformation causes silent API behavior changes for tool names with spaces. While not a crash, this is a significant UX issue — users defining tools with human-readable names containing spaces get their tool names silently changed, leading to confusing debugging sessions when tool names don't match expectations. No evidence of workflow blockage so P2 is appropriate.

source_issues.title: fix: transform_string_function_style silently transforms space-containing names without warning
source_issues.evidence: Tool names containing spaces (e.g. 'My Tool') are silently transformed to 'my_tool' without any warning being emitted. The comparison for the warning happens after the space replacement, so no warning fires for space-only transformations. Users defining tools with spaces get silent name changes, making downstream tool name mismatches hard to debug.

signals.topic: Response.output_text / responses.parse fails when output_text content item has text: null
signals.summary: Responses API can return output_text content items with text=null (e.g., from certain model outputs). The SDK's output_text property raises TypeError on null concatenation, and strict parsing rejects null values outright.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking with count=2 (two independent reporters confirming same bug): Response.output_text property raises TypeError when text=null, and strict parsing rejects the payload. Both issues have MREs. The SDK should either accept nullable output_text.text values or skip null entries gracefully.

source_issues.title: Response.output_text and responses.parse fail when an output_text item has text: null
source_issues.evidence: Strict response parsing rejects ResponseOutputText.text=null; parsed responses attempt structured parsing on null output_text causing TypeError. Two independent reporters (#3063, #3011) both confirm same failure mode with model_dump reproduction case.

source_issues.title: Response.output_text fails to handle null text values in content items
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed TypeError when accessing output_text property on Response with null text field. Separate MRE with gpt-oss-safeguard-120b model showing text:null in output_text content item.

signals.topic: Responses API undocumented reasoning+message pairing constraint + model_dump null fabrication — multi-turn conversations fail at turn 2
signals.summary: Two distinct bugs block multi-turn Responses API conversations: (1) reasoning+message items must appear as consecutive pairs in input but this is undocumented; the common pattern of filtering to only messages produces orphaned items and 400 errors. (2) model_dump() fabricates null fields (status:None, encrypted_content:None) which the API rejects as unknown parameters.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking with count=2 (two related bugs from the same reporter affecting the same workflow): multi-turn conversations — the primary use case of the Responses API — fail at turn 2 with 400 errors. OpenClaw (64.9k forks) is broken in production. Cross-SDK confirmed. Two root causes: undocumented pairing constraint and model_dump null fabrication.

source_issues.title: Responses API: undocumented reasoning+message pairing constraint breaks multi-turn conversations
source_issues.evidence: 400: Item 'msg_...' was provided without its required preceding item of type 'reasoning'. Broken in production for OpenClaw (64.9k forks). Common pattern of filtering to only message items silently produces orphaned reasoning items. Cross-SDK confirmed (Python, JS, Go, Java, .NET all fail identically).

source_issues.title: Responses API: multi-turn conversations 400 on turn 2 when passing response.output back as input
source_issues.evidence: model_dump() produces status:None, encrypted_content:None which the API rejects as 'Unknown parameter'. Turn 2 returns 400. OpenClaw (64.9k forks) broken in production. model_dump(exclude_none=True) fixes null fabrication but not the pairing constraint.

signals.topic: vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll() hangs indefinitely — file stuck at in_progress with no timeout
signals.summary: upload_and_poll() blocks forever when a vector store file gets stuck at status='in_progress'. No error, no timeout, no way to detect the failure. The raw file shows status='processed' but the vector store attachment never completes.
aliases: vector store file upload indefinite hang
vector store file stuck in_progress forever
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking: upload_and_poll() is a core user-facing API that hangs forever with no timeout, no error, and no recovery path. User cannot detect the failure state (last_error=null, status='in_progress'). This is a confirmed P0-level blocking issue with a clear MRE.

source_issues.title: `vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll()` can hang indefinitely with file status stuck at `in_progress`
source_issues.evidence: upload_and_poll() never returns; file stuck at status='in_progress' indefinitely; last_error stays null; no timeout mechanism exists; raw file already processed but vector store attachment never completes.

signals.topic: Async Responses structured outputs memory leak — unbounded pydantic SchemaValidator allocation causing OOM
signals.summary: responses.parse() allocates a new SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer (heavy Rust objects) on every single call because Pydantic cannot resolve a free TypeVar, causing linear RSS growth and eventual OOM in long-running servers.
signals.review_reason: Critical reliability issue: long-running server processes accumulate unbounded memory via SchemaValidator allocations on every responses.parse() call, inevitably leading to OOM. Flame graph evidence provided. The bug is in openai/lib/_parsing/_responses.py and has a clear fix (use non-parameterized base classes). This is a production-blocking issue for any server using structured outputs.

source_issues.title: Async Responses Structured Outputs Memory leak
source_issues.evidence: Flame graph attached showing linear RSS growth. Root cause: construct_type_unchecked called with TypeVar-subscripted generics, model_rebuild always returns False for unresolved TypeVar, cache never populated, new SchemaValidator/Serializer allocated per call. In production long-running servers, process will eventually OOM.

signals.topic: Batch API returns 404 for GPT-5.x models — invalid -batch suffix appended to model name
signals.summary: Using /v1/chat/completions endpoint with GPT-5.x models via Batch API results in 404 because the backend appends an invalid '-batch' suffix (e.g., gpt-5-2025-08-07-batch) that does not exist. GPT-4.x models work correctly with the same code.
signals.review_reason: Significant production impact: batch API — a key cost-saving feature for high-volume workloads — is completely broken for all GPT-5.x models. The root cause is an invalid '-batch' suffix appended by the backend. While the fix likely involves backend changes, the SDK needs to handle or surface this error better rather than letting 100% of batch requests fail silently.

source_issues.title: OpenAI Batch API returns 404 with GPT-5.x models
source_issues.evidence: Batch API with GPT-5.4-mini via /v1/chat/completions returns 404 model_not_found for 'gpt-5-2025-08-07-batch'. Same code with gpt-4o returns 200. The batch model does not exist. All GPT-5.x models affected.

signals.topic: Persistent ACP session adapter exits after every turn instead of being pooled, causing repeated cold-start costs
signals.summary: In the `runTurn` finally block, `client.close()` is called unconditionally without a symmetric path to return the persistent client to `pendingPersistentClients`. This means every turn on a persistent session kills the adapter process, and the next turn pays the full cold-start cost again (23s for Claude CLI, 74–112s for Gemini CLI). `acp.runtime.ttlMinutes` is also ineffective because the adapter dies after each turn regardless of TTL.
aliases: persistent client not returned to pool
ACP adapter torn down every turn
persistent session cold-start on every send
signals.review_reason: Root cause is clearly identified in manager.ts L519 where client.close() unconditionally terminates the persistent adapter after every turn. This is a lifecycle asymmetry bug that directly causes: (1) repeated full cold-start latency on every turn — 23s for Claude, 74-112s for Gemini; (2) wasted compute cost from re-spawning adapters instead of reusing pooled ones; (3) `ttlMinutes` setting becomes a no-op for persistent sessions. All ACP agents (claude-acp, gemini-acp) are affected. The proposed fix is validated locally and is minimal.

source_issues.title: [bug] persistent ACP client not returned to pool after runTurn
source_issues.evidence: Persistent ACP sessions pay a full cold-start cost on every `sessions_send`. `acp.runtime.ttlMinutes` has no effect on adapter process longevity. Reproduction shows PID 104981 (gemini CLI) exits after turn 1; turn 2 re-spawns it with full cold-start (~74-112s). Local validation confirms fix retains same PID across turns with warm path latency.

signals.topic: Creating a new codex session via `acpx codex sessions new` fails to register with codex CLI — `codex resume` cannot find the session
signals.summary: When a user creates a new codex session with `acpx codex sessions new`, the session is created and recorded by acpx, but codex CLI itself does not save or recognize the session. Calling `codex resume <session_id>` immediately after creation returns 'No saved session found'. This works correctly for kimi but is broken for codex, making session persistence across CLI invocations unusable for the codex agent.
aliases: codex session not found after acpx sessions new
codex resume fails with No saved session found
signals.review_reason: Core session persistence functionality is broken for the codex agent: users cannot resume sessions they just created via acpx. The session ID is generated and recorded by acpx, but codex itself does not persist the session, making `codex resume` fail. This is a main-flow failure for the codex agent. The same flow works correctly for kimi, confirming this is a codex-specific regression. Blocking for any workflow that uses `acpx codex sessions new` followed by `codex resume`.

source_issues.title: new codex session 后，并没有注册到 codex 的 session，kimi 是没问题的
source_issues.evidence: Exact reproduction: `acpx codex sessions new --name test` succeeds and outputs a session ID, but `codex resume <id>` immediately returns 'No saved session found with ID'. Same flow works with `kimi` agent. Issue has 1 comment, confirming active user scenario.

signals.topic: QuietOutputFormatter silently discards token usage and cost, making consumption tracking impossible without switching to JSON format
signals.summary: When using `--format quiet`, token usage fields (inputTokens, outputTokens, cachedReadTokens, cachedWriteTokens, totalTokens) and cost are completely discarded — they appear in neither stdout nor stderr. Callers (CI runners, orchestrators, billing dashboards) cannot track API consumption without switching to `--format json`, which changes the stdout contract entirely.
aliases: token usage not emitted to stderr in quiet mode
signals.review_reason: While technically a feature request, the described behavior actively prevents observability for legitimate CI and billing workflows. The issue explicitly identifies affected callers (CI runners, orchestrators, billing dashboards) who have no viable workaround without switching output format. Token usage data is already available in `message.result` at the stop-reason flush point but is silently ignored, making this a UX/integration gap rather than a pure enhancement. P2 because there is no reported production failure caused by this gap — it is an integration limitation.

source_issues.title: feat: QuietOutputFormatter silently discards token usage — emit to stderr
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction steps show `--format quiet --verbose` produces no token/cost output in stdout or stderr, while `--format json` includes full usage in the JSON-RPC response. Root cause: `onAcpMessage` only handles text chunks and stop reason; `message.result.usage` is never read even though `parsePromptStopReason` already parses `message.result` at that point. Errors are also silently dropped via `onError(_params) {}`.

signals.topic: VirusTotal Code Insight false positive flags block legitimate skill installations in CI/Docker/MCP non-interactive environments
signals.summary: VirusTotal Code Insight heuristics (crypto-key patterns, WebSocket, minified JS, external API calls, divination keywords) are triggering false-positive 'suspicious'/'malicious' verdicts on legitimate skills across diverse domains (trading SDKs, IM plugins, document tools, observability tools). In non-interactive mode, `clawhub install` hard-fails with a blocking error requiring `--force`, which is unknown to many users and unsuitable for automated environments (CI, Docker, MCP server bootstraps). Multiple publishers have filed appeals with no resolution, and recent internal commits acknowledge this as an ongoing false-positive problem.
aliases: VirusTotal heuristic false positive blocks skill install
suspicious flag false positive on legitimate skills
signals.review_reason: P0: 10 distinct issues from 8 unique publishers all reporting the same root cause — VT Code Insight heuristics generating false-positive 'suspicious'/'malicious' verdicts on legitimate skills. User impact is clearly blocking: `clawhub install` hard-fails in CI/Docker/MCP non-interactive environments with a binding error. Issue #1787 explicitly documents the error message, quantifies impact (14 skills, 8.3k downloads, active since February), and references recent internal commits acknowledging this as an ongoing tuning problem. The diversity of falsely-flagged skill types (trading SDKs, IM plugins, doc tools, divination skills, observability tools) confirms this is a systemic platform issue, not isolated. Publishers cannot distribute their skills — this is a critical distribution/blocking pain point.

signals.topic: system.run command execution allows env variable injection and shell wrapper approval bypass
signals.summary: The system.run implementation has two security gaps: (1) arbitrary env vars (GIT_SSH_COMMAND, NODE_OPTIONS, LD_PRELOAD, BASH_ENV, etc.) are passed through to ProcessStartInfo without sanitization, allowing connected agents to silently alter command behavior after approval; (2) shell wrappers (bash -c, cmd /c, powershell -Command, pwsh -Command) are only evaluated at the outer command level, letting inner destructive payloads bypass exec approval rules.
aliases: exec policy bypass via env vars
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point: the exec approval system can be bypassed through env var injection (e.g. GIT_SSH_COMMAND, NODE_OPTIONS, LD_PRELOAD) or via shell wrapper payloads, allowing a connected agent to execute commands outside the scope of what was approved. The core security boundary of the command execution system is broken. While it affects only 1 issue, the impact is architectural and high-severity (arbitrary command execution), and it directly undermines the product's access-control model. The review_reason cannot rest on count alone when the severity and scope are this significant.

source_issues.title: [Security] system.run: env variable injection and shell wrapper approval bypass
source_issues.evidence: A connected agent can submit a command approved as 'git status' but inject GIT_SSH_COMMAND='evil.sh' to alter execution. Similarly, 'powershell -Command Remove-Item -Recurse -Force C:\important' can bypass rules blocking Remove-Item if the outer 'powershell *' is allowed. The LocalCommandRunner directly copies the request env dict into ProcessStartInfo.Environment with no sanitization (SystemCapability.cs:266/303, LocalCommandRunner.cs:52). Policy evaluation happens once on the outer command before execution (SystemCapability.cs:293). No coverage exists for wrapper forms in existing tests.

signals.topic: SIGUSR1 supervisor restart fails silently — gateway left dead, no in-band recovery path
signals.summary: When update.run triggers a supervisor restart via SIGUSR1, re-exec failures cause process exit with code 0. systemd's Restart=on-failure treats this as clean exit and does not relaunch, leaving gateway dead for extended periods with no in-band recovery.

source_issues.title: Gateway left dead after update.run / SIGUSR1 supervisor restart — systemd sees clean exit, does not relaunch
source_issues.evidence: Deterministically hit on two separate nodes on 2026-04-22. Both stayed down for ~19 hours. User sees 502 Bad Gateway. Recovery requires SSH + systemctl --user restart. Control UI cannot self-fix because it needs the gateway. Reproduced on Oracle Cloud Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64.

signals.topic: Git pre-commit hooks bypassed by default at runtime (--no-verify) — security policy enforcement failure
signals.summary: Aider's default commit path uses --no-verify, bypassing all pre-commit hooks including security controls (secret scanning, dangerous pattern blocking). Users explicitly relying on hooks for security policy enforcement have no protection.
aliases: git commit verify false by default
signals.review_reason: Security trust boundary violation: pre-commit hooks used for secret scanning and policy enforcement are silently bypassed by default. Attacker can exfiltrate secrets or bypass security policies without any warning. Clearly impacts real security workflows.

source_issues.title: Default runtime commits bypass pre-commit hooks via --no-verify
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible: manual git commit with subprocess.check_output pattern blocked by hook; Aider commits same pattern successfully. Pre-commit hooks used for secret scanning and security enforcement are silently bypassed. --git-commit-verify defaults to False.

signals.topic: UI and SQLite persist API keys / Bearer tokens in plain text, causing credential leaks on share or machine compromise
signals.summary: promptfoo's UI Details panel and SQLite eval history store rendered provider configs verbatim, including Authorization headers and API keys, leading to credential leakage when users share debug info or if the machine is compromised.
aliases: Bearer token leak in eval history
credential stored in plaintext in SQLite
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed credential-leak vulnerability with clear user impact: (1) users copy-paste debug blobs to share with teammates/vendors/forums and silently leak live credentials inline with config data; (2) any local user or malware with SQLite read access retrieves all API keys ever used; (3) exported evals and shared URLs propagate credentials. The issue is reproducible, has a clear root cause, and the blast radius includes both intentional sharing and passive local access. No workaround exists that doesn't compromise the core eval workflow.

source_issues.title: UI and stored eval record expose rendered Authorization / apiKey in plain text
source_issues.evidence: UI Details panel and ~/.promptfoo/promptfoo.db store rendered provider configs verbatim. Credentials end up in eval exports, shared eval URLs, and SQLite history regardless of user awareness. A user sharing a debug blob with a teammate, vendor, or public forum leaks a live credential. Anyone with access to the machine gets every credential ever evaluated against.

signals.topic: OpenRouter provider silently ignores user-supplied apiBaseUrl, breaking proxy/compliance-gateway setups
signals.summary: The OpenRouterProvider hardcodes apiBaseUrl after spreading user config, so any user-supplied apiBaseUrl in promptfooconfig.yaml is silently discarded. Users routing OpenRouter through a corporate proxy or compliance gateway get 401 errors with no indication the config is ignored.
signals.review_reason: User-configured apiBaseUrl is silently discarded with no warning, causing opaque 401 errors. This blocks enterprise users who route OpenRouter through a compliance gateway or caching proxy — a legitimate and common enterprise setup. The absence of any error or log about the override means users waste significant time debugging before discovering the config is ignored. While count=1, the enterprise use case and complete lack of fallback behavior warrant P1.

source_issues.title: openrouter provider: hardcoded apiBaseUrl silently overrides user config
source_issues.evidence: Source verified: OpenRouterProvider super() call spreads providerOptions.config first, then overwrites apiBaseUrl with the hardcoded URL. Repro shows user-supplied apiBaseUrl is dropped. Observed as unexpected 401 from proxy or packet capture with no indication the config was ignored.

signals.topic: GET /eval/:id/table crashes with RangeError for large evals, blocking the web UI
signals.summary: The eval table endpoint crashes with an unhandled RangeError when JSON.stringify() exceeds V8's ~512MB string limit, which occurs routinely with base64-encoded images or large prompt content. Users cannot view eval results in the UI for large evals.
aliases: eval table 500 error on large payloads
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed crash (500 error) that blocks the primary UI workflow for any eval with moderately large outputs. Base64 images in prompt evaluation are a legitimate and common use case, making this a recurring failure mode. The issue was reproducible and required a dedicated fix (#7599), confirming it was a real blocker. Users lose visibility into eval results — the core value proposition of the tool.

source_issues.title: RangeError crash on GET /eval/:id/table for large evals
source_issues.evidence: Endpoint returns 500 error and UI fails to load results when eval has large outputs (e.g. base64 images, 200 test cases with images). Root cause is unhandled RangeError from JSON.stringify exceeding V8's ~512MB limit. No error handling existed for this case.

signals.topic: TypeScript enum not supported in strip-only mode blocks embedding promptfoo into user projects
signals.summary: Users integrating promptfoo as a library into their TypeScript frontend project encounter 'TypeScript enum is not supported in strip-only mode' errors and 'Cannot find package' module resolution failures when running eval, preventing library embedding entirely.
signals.review_reason: This is a complete workflow blocker for users attempting to embed promptfoo as a library in their own TypeScript projects. The user cannot run eval at all — neither in default mode nor with the experimental flag. This prevents a legitimate and growing use case (running evaluations programmatically within a larger system). Two distinct errors compound the problem: the TypeScript enum limitation and the module resolution failure.

source_issues.title: Integrating Promptfoo with a Frontend TypeScript Project
source_issues.evidence: User wrote a custom provider using the promptfoo library in a TypeScript frontend project. Running 'npx promptfoo eval' produces 'TypeScript enum is not supported in strip-only mode' error. Workaround with NODE_OPTIONS='--experimental-transform-types' produces 'ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package @/utils' error. eval cannot run at all.

signals.topic: llm-rubric assertions in defaultTest cannot resolve {{varName}} template variables, breaking per-case evaluation
signals.summary: When llm-rubric assertions are defined in defaultTest, template variables like {{input}} are not resolved — the rubric receives literal strings like '{{input}}' instead of the actual variable value. This prevents defaultTest rubrics from performing meaningful per-case evaluation.
aliases: llm-rubric template variables not resolved in defaultTest
defaultTest rubric receives literal template strings
template variable resolution missing in defaultTest assertions
signals.review_reason: Template variable resolution failure in defaultTest is a real functional degradation: users who define assertions centrally in defaultTest (the intended pattern for uniform evaluation across test cases) cannot use variable-aware rubrics, forcing a complex workaround. The issue was reproducible and closed with acknowledgment. While count=1, the workaround is non-obvious and the pattern is central to promptfoo's evaluation design. Lowered to P2 because the workaround exists and it is not a crash or complete workflow block.

source_issues.title: llm-rubric assertions in defaultTest cannot access test case variables via {{varName}} template syntax
source_issues.evidence: Rubric defined in defaultTest receives literal '{{myVar}}' instead of resolved value 'hello world'. The same rubric works correctly when defined inline per test case. User has no way to reference per-case variables in defaultTest rubrics without a complex transform workaround. This is described as a 'significant limitation' for a core feature.

signals.topic: QueryFusionRetriever reciprocal_rerank mode silently ignores retriever_weights
signals.summary: When using mode='reciprocal_rerank', the QueryFusionRetriever silently ignores the retriever_weights parameter, treating all retrievers equally regardless of configured weights. This causes incorrect fused ranking results in production RAG pipelines.
signals.review_reason: Single reported bug but impact is clear: retriever weights are silently ignored, causing incorrect ranking in multi-retriever RAG pipelines. User-experienced behavior (wrong results) is documented with a full reproducer. Marked P2 because count=1 and only affects reciprocal_rerank mode specifically.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: QueryFusionRetriever ignores `retriever_weights` when `mode="reciprocal_rerank"`
source_issues.evidence: retriever_weights=[1.0, 0.0] with two retrievers returns results from both, proving weights are silently ignored. All retrievers are equally weighted in fused score. Reproducer provided showing weight=0.0 retriever still contributes results.

source_issues.evidence: TreeSelectLeafRetriever query path returns empty source_nodes, breaking citation and traceability. User cannot identify which source documents contributed to results.

signals.review_reason: Single bug causing in-place state mutation that corrupts caller objects. Triggers silently when event telemetry is active, leading to unpredictable downstream failures. Clear user impact on data integrity. Marked P2 due to count=1.
