source_issues.evidence: model_dump() mutates ChatResponse.raw in-place, corrupting the caller's response object when telemetry/event handling is enabled. In-place mutation causes unpredictable downstream failures.

signals.topic: to_openai_message_dict doesn't JSON-serialize ToolCallBlock.tool_kwargs breaking cross-provider agent workflows
signals.summary: When Anthropic tool calls (using ToolCallBlock) are passed to an OpenAI-compatible provider, to_openai_message_dict fails to JSON-serialize tool_kwargs, causing API errors and breaking cross-provider agent workflows.
signals.review_reason: Cross-provider agent workflow breakage is a high-impact issue for users building multi-model agent pipelines. JSON-serialization failure causes API errors that are hard to debug. Prioritized P1 despite count=1 because the cross-provider pattern is explicitly documented as a supported use case.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: to_openai_message_dict doesn't JSON-serialize ToolCallBlock.tool_kwargs and breaks cross-provider agent workflows
source_issues.evidence: to_openai_message_dict doesn't JSON-serialize ToolCallBlock.tool_kwargs, causing API errors when Anthropic tool calls are forwarded to OpenAI-compatible providers. Cross-provider agent workflows break.

signals.topic: Falsy metadata values (0, false, empty string, empty list) stored as None in Azure AI Search index causing data corruption
signals.summary: When indexing documents with falsy metadata values (0, '', false, []), Azure AI Search indexer treats them as null/None, causing data loss and incorrect filtering/querying results for users relying on metadata fidelity.
aliases: Azure AI Search falsy metadata stored as None
Azure AI Search metadata data loss
signals.review_reason: Silent data corruption in a specific integration (Azure AI Search) where falsy values are replaced with None. Data loss is a clear user impact affecting metadata-dependent queries. Marked P2 due to count=1 and single integration scope.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: falsy metadata values stored as None in Azure AI Search index
source_issues.evidence: Falsy metadata values (0, false, '', []) are stored as None in Azure AI Search index. This causes data corruption where valid zero/empty values are lost and replaced with null. Affects filtering and querying.

signals.topic: Windows: daemon start/status broken — Unix `ps -o pid` command fails on Windows
signals.summary: On Windows (Git Bash/msys2), `daemon start` silently dies within ~2s and `daemon status` reports STOPPED because the tool calls Unix-style `ps -o pid` syntax that Windows `ps` does not support.
aliases: daemon process health check fails on Windows
signals.review_reason: Two independent reporters confirm daemon start silently dies and daemon status always shows STOPPED on Windows due to Unix `ps` syntax. This is a main-flow blocker for ALL Windows users — background daemon cannot be reliably used. High confidence, high impact.

source_issues.title: daemon start silently dies on Windows due to ps -o incompatibility
source_issues.evidence: On Windows Git Bash, `ps: unknown option -- o` causes daemon to exit within ~2s with no log output. Confirmed on both v3.5.7 and v3.5.80. Blocks all background daemon usage on Windows.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Daemon status shows STOPPED on Windows — ps -o pid command not supported
source_issues.evidence: Same `ps -o pid` failure on Windows causes `daemon status` to always report STOPPED even when daemon process is actively running. Misleading status for all Windows operators.

signals.topic: Session save crashes with TypeError and session list renders corrupted rows
signals.summary: ruflo session save crashes with TypeError when no swarm is active, causing partial/corrupt writes. ruflo session list then reads those corrupt files and renders empty rows with 'Invalid Date' timestamps.
aliases: session schema drift reader vs writer
signals.review_reason: Two issues confirm the same bug: session save throws TypeError and leaves corrupt partial records; session list then reads corrupt data and renders garbage rows. Blocks session persistence entirely for non-swarm use cases and corrupts the session registry. High impact, clear evidence.

source_issues.title: ruflo/claude-flow session save crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading agentCount)'; session list shows corrupt Invalid Date rows
source_issues.evidence: session save writes partial record then throws TypeError. session list renders ~10 rows with empty ID, name='-', and 'Invalid Date In...' timestamps. session current reports 'No active session' immediately after save.

source_issues.title: CLI v3.5.80: session-end hang, session save TypeError, session list broken rendering
source_issues.evidence: Confirms session save TypeError when no swarm is active. session list renders broken table with empty rows and 'Invalid Date In...' timestamps. Additionally session-end summary renders undefined counters. Root cause: missing null guard on swarm metrics object.

signals.topic: hooks post-task and session-end hang indefinitely after completing work
signals.summary: ruflo hooks post-task and ruflo hooks session-end both complete their functional work (writing state to disk) but the Node process never exits, holding open handles (memory.db) until externally killed.
signals.review_reason: Two separate hooks commands (post-task, session-end) both exhibit the same hang pattern: work completes, state is persisted, but process never exits due to unclosed async handles. Blocks CI pipelines and slash commands that expect synchronous execution. Clear user impact confirmed by multiple reporters.

source_issues.title: ruflo hooks post-task hangs indefinitely after recording outcome (v3.5.80)
source_issues.evidence: post-task records outcome in ~1s but process hangs indefinitely at 0% CPU holding memory.db open. All stdin variations tested produce the same hang. Confirmed by timeout command that SIGTERM is the only exit path. Blocks slash commands and CI scripts.

source_issues.title: CLI v3.5.80: session-end hang, session save TypeError, session list broken rendering
source_issues.evidence: session-end writes session JSON to disk successfully then hangs forever at 0% CPU. lsof shows process still holds memory.db open (fd 18 RW). Confirmed hanging for 4+ minutes. Same unclosed handle pattern as post-task hang.

signals.topic: MCP hooks_worker-dispatch and workflow_run report fabricated success without executing real work
signals.summary: MCP hooks_worker-dispatch returns 'completed' status but does not route to the daemon's real worker implementations — runCount does not increment. workflow_run returns zero agentsSpawned even on live invocations. process workers --action list returns hardcoded demo IDs not matching the real daemon registry.
aliases: process workers list hardcoded demo IDs
signals.review_reason: MCP dispatch and workflow_run surfaces return success/completion signals without actually executing the requested workers. This is not a mere cosmetic bug — CI pipelines and MCP-driven automations relying on these surfaces will silently skip work and assume tasks completed. Clear evidence that daemon trigger DOES work, proving the real pipeline is wired; the MCP surfaces are disconnected stubs.

source_issues.title: MCP hooks_worker-dispatch returns fabricated completion independent of daemon; process workers --action list returns hardcoded demo IDs
source_issues.evidence: MCP hooks_worker-dispatch returns status:completed in <1s but daemon runCount is unchanged — no real worker executed. workflow_run returns agentsSpawned:0 for both dryRun:true and dryRun:false. process workers list returns hardcoded demo IDs not matching daemon-state.json. This is a reporting-vs-execution defect in core automation surfaces.

signals.topic: daemon-state.json write race — background daemon flush clobbers CLI-trigger increments
signals.summary: When a background daemon and a concurrent CLI trigger both write to daemon-state.json, the background daemon's periodic flush overwrites the CLI's increment, making persisted runCount appear unchanged even though the work executed.
aliases: daemon state file write race condition
runCount increment lost to background flush
concurrent daemon-state.json writes clobber each other
signals.review_reason: Write race on daemon-state.json causes runCount increments to be silently lost — operators monitoring persisted state will conclude that daemon triggers failed to execute when they actually ran. This is a data integrity issue that breaks operational monitoring and trust in the daemon pipeline. Verified with detailed repro on Windows and Linux.

source_issues.title: daemon-state.json write-race: background daemon's periodic in-memory flush can overwrite atomic runCount increments from ruflo daemon trigger --worker
source_issues.evidence: Verified locally: CLI trigger increments runCount to 433, real-time probe shows correct value, but background daemon's next flush reverts it to 432. Operators using persisted-state checks conclude triggers failed when work actually ran. Full repro steps and five fix categories provided.

signals.topic: CDP connection silently fails when external Chrome browser restarts
signals.summary: When connecting to an external Chrome via CDP (--cdp / connect command), closing and reopening Chrome generates a new webSocketDebuggerUrl UUID, but agent-browser daemon does not rediscover the new URL and silently fails, leaving users unable to reconnect to their external browser session.
signals.review_reason: 阻断主流程：用户依赖CDP连接外部Chrome以保留session/cookie，复用profile。当Chrome重启后完全无法重连，无错误提示，导致CDP工作流完全失效。用户已定位到源码级根因（cli/src/main.rs第985行daemon跳过reconnect逻辑）。

source_issues.title: CDP connection fails silently when external browser restarts (new webSocketDebuggerUrl)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: daemon skips CDP launch command when already running, continues using stale webSocketDebuggerUrl UUID. Impact: users lose CDP session after any Chrome restart, no error thrown.

signals.topic: agent-browser open command hangs indefinitely on Windows Git Bash
signals.summary: On Windows 11 + Git Bash, the 'agent browser open' command hangs indefinitely with no stdout or error on every URL. This is a complete workflow blocker for the primary command with no workaround — even after OS reboot and clean state.
aliases: open command blocks forever on Windows
signals.review_reason: 阻断主流程：'open'是agent-browser最基础最核心的命令，hang导致整个验证流程挂起。用户已排除所有常规原因（zombie进程、stale文件、重启），且同一天早期同一环境可以工作，说明是代码路径问题而非配置问题。Windows用户无任何workaround。

source_issues.title: open <url> hangs indefinitely on Windows Git Bash (post-reboot + clean pid files, no Chromium zombies)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed hangs on every URL including https://example.com, after full OS reboot, with zero stale pid/port files. Hypothesized root cause: Chromium/Playwright-launcher synchronous wait on Windows named pipes. User's verification gate completely stalled.

signals.topic: Chrome killed after ~7s idle due to PR_SET_PDEATHSIG tokio regression (v0.24.1)
signals.summary: v0.24.1 introduced PR_SET_PDEATHSIG in Chrome's pre_exec hook which causes Chrome to be killed after ~7-9 seconds idle on every site, because tokio's multi-threaded runtime recycles the worker thread that called fork(). All pages navigate to about:blank, downloads break, and any automation longer than 7 seconds fails.
signals.review_reason: 显著影响用户体验和主流程：任何超过7秒的自动化工作流（包括多步骤下载、内容抓取验证）全部失败，Chrome静默重启导致页面跳转到about:blank，用户无感知原因。已有用户级源码分析和一个备用fix验证。虽然issue已修复合并，但数据窗口内仍有用户受影响历史记录。

source_issues.title: fix: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG kills Chrome in tokio multi-threaded runtime (v0.24.1 regression)
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced on zero-custom-args v0.24.1 binary, every site, both headless and headed. download workflows completely broken (2nd download fails). Proposed sentinel-process fix validated by reporter. Issue closed 2026-04-13.

signals.topic: Snapshot serializer strips whitespace around React JSX comment nodes causing false-positive a11y/text errors for AI agents
signals.summary: When a React/Next.js page renders JSX whitespace expressions like {' '}, the compiled HTML contains <!-- --> comment nodes. The snapshot text serializer strips both the comment and adjacent whitespace text nodes, causing StaticText to concatenate without spaces (e.g., 'yesterday.Two' instead of 'yesterday. Two'). This generates false-positive typo/a11y bug reports for AI agents reading snapshots.
aliases: React JSX whitespace comment stripped in snapshot
snapshot StaticText concatenates without space around HTML comments
signals.review_reason: 明显体验下降：AI agent依赖snapshot做内容验证，误报导致浪费调查轮次（turns），且影响所有使用React/Next.js标准JSX语法的网站（标准React输出模式）。已通过真实dogfood session验证影响。

source_issues.title: Snapshot text serializer strips whitespace around HTML comments (JSX {' '} false-positive)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed in dogfood session: agent surfaced 'ISSUE-001 typo/a11y bug' — investigation revealed site renders correctly but snapshot serializer stripped whitespace across React comment boundaries. Affects all Next.js 15 apps using JSX whitespace between siblings.

signals.topic: Click command silently succeeds on invisible/off-screen elements without error
signals.summary: When an element is not visible in the viewport (requires scroll to be seen), 'agent-browser click' completes without error but has no effect on the page. Users cannot tell whether the click succeeded, leading to unreliable automation and false confidence in agent workflows.
aliases: click succeeds silently on invisible elements
off-screen element click has no effect
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可靠：click是agent-browser核心操作，silent failure导致自动化结果不可信，agent无法判断是否真正完成操作，存在假阳性信任风险。

source_issues.title: Clicking an invisible element with agent-browser seems to have no effect, yet the command doesn't throw an error？
source_issues.evidence: User reported that snapshot lists elements not visible until scrolled, and clicking them completes with exit code 0 but nothing happens. No error, no indication of failure. Viewport enlargement via 'set viewport' zooms instead of resizing.

signals.topic: 用户发送消息后遇到通用错误 'Oops, an error occurred!'，主流程阻断
signals.summary: 用户在使用聊天机器人发送消息时，反复遇到通用的 'Oops, an error occurred!' 错误提示，导致对话流程完全无法进行。该错误信息缺乏具体原因，用户无法自行诊断和解决。
signals.review_reason: Issue #1488 有明确用户影响证据：用户主流程（发送消息）被通用错误阻断，附截图证明。但因 count=1、缺乏根因信息、错误描述泛化，置信度受限，故评级为 P2 而非 P0。该痛点落在用户可感知场景（聊天消息发送），符合保留标准。

source_issues.title: Well it doesn't work it always says : Oops, an error occurred!
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告聊天界面发送消息后持续显示通用错误 'Oops, an error occurred!'，附带截图佐证，主流程阻断，无法完成任何对话交互

signals.topic: xAI/Grok tool calling broken: `addAdditionalPropertiesToJsonSchema` injects `additionalProperties: false` that xAI rejects
signals.summary: All xAI/Grok tool calls fail with HTTP 400 'false is not supported' because the SDK forcibly adds `additionalProperties: false` to object schemas, even though xAI's validator rejects this. No workaround short of disabling tools entirely.
signals.review_reason: Tool calling is a core use case; xAI users cannot use tools at all without a workaround that disables the feature. Clear API error, reproduction provided, root cause identified.

source_issues.title: addAdditionalPropertiesToJsonSchema breaks xAI/Grok tool calling: xAI rejects additionalProperties: false
source_issues.evidence: All xAI/Grok tool calls fail with 'Schema validation failed: property schema false is not supported'. Workaround disables tools entirely.

signals.topic: Streamable HTTP MCP transport does not downgrade `mcp-protocol-version` header after version negotiation, breaking Figma Dev Mode and other version-constrained MCP servers
signals.summary: After MCP initialize negotiation returns a lower protocol version, the HTTP transport keeps sending the latest version in the header on all follow-up requests, causing 400 rejections. Affected servers include Figma Dev Mode MCP Server.
aliases: MCP protocol version header not downgraded
MCP HTTP transport version negotiation bug
signals.review_reason: MCP client initialization completely fails against any MCP server that negotiates down a protocol version. Main flow (MCP client creation) is blocked. Real-world impact confirmed with Figma Dev Mode MCP Server.

source_issues.title: [@ai-sdk/mcp] Streamable HTTP transport does not downgrade `mcp-protocol-version` header after version negotiation (breaks servers like Figma Dev Mode MCP)
source_issues.evidence: createMCPClient() never resolves; follow-up notifications/initialized request returns HTTP 400 'Unsupported protocol version'. Author validated fix via pnpm patch. Affects both @ai-sdk/mcp 1.x and 2.x-beta.

signals.topic: useChat/useUIStream resume after network blip or proxy timeout duplicates text and reasoning parts in the UI
signals.summary: When resumeStream replays a buffered UIMessageStream against a message with pre-existing parts, `text-start` and `reasoning-start` handlers push duplicate parts instead of reusing existing ones. User-visible effect: UI flashes and duplicate content on network blips, lifecycle aborts, or proxy timeouts.
signals.review_reason: Core streaming UI is affected. Any network blip, lifecycle abort, or proxy timeout during a streaming session causes visible UI flashes and duplicated content, which is a significant UX degradation for the primary use case.

source_issues.title: useChat resume duplicates `text` and `reasoning` parts when replaying UIMessage stream
source_issues.evidence: Test cases confirm 'expected length 1 but got 2'. Bug present in ai@6.x and 7.0.0-beta.111. User-visible UI flash and duplicate content. Author ships workaround via pnpm patch.

signals.topic: Vertex AI rejects `includeServerSideToolInvocations` field on Gemini 3.x function tools, blocking all such requests
signals.summary: The Google-vertex provider hard-codes `includeServerSideToolInvocations: true` in the combined tool config for Gemini 3-or-newer + function tools, but Vertex's preview endpoint now hard-rejects unknown fields with HTTP 400. All Vertex + Gemini 3.x + function tools requests fail.
signals.review_reason: Production Vertex deployments with Gemini 3.x and function tools are completely broken. This is a main-flow failure for Google-vertex provider users, with no path forward without downgrading or disabling tools.

source_issues.title: Title: @ai-sdk/google: Vertex rejects tool_config.includeServerSideToolInvocations on gemini-3-flash-preview with function tools
source_issues.evidence: Every Vertex request to gemini-3-*-preview with function tools fails with HTTP 400 'Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name includeServerSideToolInvocations at tool_config'. Workaround is downgrading to gemini-2.5.

signals.topic: streamText with tool calls and maxSteps > 1 in Node.js streaming context silently truncates response after first tool invocation
signals.summary: When using streamText with tools and maxSteps > 1 in a Node.js server context (e.g. Next.js API Route), the stream terminates after the first tool call without any error. The full multi-step generation never completes and the client receives a truncated stream silently.
signals.review_reason: Core streaming functionality breaks silently in the most common deployment scenario (Node.js server with multi-step tool calls). No error is thrown, making this hard to debug. Main flow is blocked.

source_issues.title: streamText response stops mid-generation when used with tool calls and maxSteps > 1 in Node.js streaming context
source_issues.evidence: Stream cuts off silently after first tool step without any error in Next.js API Route context. Full multi-step generation fails to complete.

signals.topic: Build fails on Node 25 with prerender errors in Next.js 15 and 16 scaffolds
signals.summary: Fresh create-next-app scaffold fails next build on Node 25.4.0. Next 15 fails with 'Html should not be imported outside of pages/_document'. Next 16 fails with 'Cannot read properties of null (reading useContext)' during prerender of /_global-error. Builds cleanly on Node 20.
signals.review_reason: Multiple distinct build failures block production deployments: Node 25 incompatibility (affecting new scaffolding), _global-error prerender crash (blocking 16.2.4 builds), and shared hosting WASM memory limits. Combined, these prevent builds in real deployment environments.

source_issues.title: next build fails on Node 25 during prerender (Next 15 and 16 scaffolds)
source_issues.evidence: Fresh create-next-app fails next build on Node 25.4.0 with distinct errors per version. Builds cleanly on Node 20. Users on Node 25 cannot build Next.js apps at all.

source_issues.title: Next 16.2.4: next build crashes prerendering /_global-error with TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useContext')
source_issues.evidence: next build on fresh create-next-app@16.2.4 crashes during prerender of /_global-error. Pinning next@16.3.0-canary.2 resolves it. Confirmed build-time crash.

source_issues.title: Next.js build fails with 'WebAssembly.instantiate(): Out of memory' on shared hosting (O2switch / cPanel)
source_issues.evidence: Build fails with RangeError: WebAssembly.instantiate(): Out of memory: wasm memory on shared hosting with cPanel. Works locally and on VPS/Vercel. Blocks deployment on specific hosting environments.

signals.topic: Non-ASCII dynamic route params cause 500 errors in App Router due to x-next-cache-tags header validation
signals.summary: When App Router dynamic routes contain non-ASCII characters (Hebrew, Arabic, Chinese, emoji in slugs), every request returns 500 because Next.js writes the raw path into the RFC-7230 ASCII-only x-next-cache-tags HTTP header without encoding, triggering Node's validateHeaderValue. No workaround works reliably.
signals.review_reason: Blocks ISR for any non-ASCII slug (Hebrew/Arabic/CJK/emoji) completely. Returns 500 on every affected route with no reliable workaround. Root cause is clear (header encoding missing) and affects production deployments on Vercel.

source_issues.title: App Router: non-ASCII dynamic route params crash with ERR_INVALID_CHAR on x-next-cache-tags header
source_issues.evidence: Reproduces with curl to Hebrew/Arabic/Chinese slugs -> 500 Internal Server Error. TypeError: Invalid character in header content [x-next-cache-tags] code: ERR_INVALID_CHAR. Applies to both local dev and Vercel production deployment. Statically pre-rendered pages via generateStaticParams are also affected at request time.

signals.topic: Memory leak in Next.js 16.2.4 stable causes production OOM crashes — fix exists in canary but not released
signals.summary: Memory leak (tee'd response clone FinalizationRegistry + LRU minimum size, fixed in canary PRs #88577/#89040) is absent from 16.x stable for 45+ days. Production services slowly accumulate arrayBuffers until OOM. A Render service hits 512 MiB cap in ~8 hours.
signals.review_reason: Direct production impact: services crash with OOM within hours. The fix is known and in canary, but users on stable are left without it for 45+ days. This is a severe resource leak that blocks production workloads.

source_issues.title: Memory leak fix from canary (PRs #88577, #89040) still not in any 16.x stable release 45+ days later — production OOMs ongoing on 16.2.4
source_issues.evidence: Production service on Render accumulates arrayBuffers over time until hitting 512 MiB OOM cap in approximately 8 hours. Fix PRs exist in canary (#88577, #89040) but stable release 16.2.4 is missing them for 45+ days. No workaround available for users on stable.

signals.topic: next/image in dev mode shows stale image after editing local file with same filename — requires manual .next deletion
signals.summary: When editing a local image file without changing its filename, next/image displays a stale version while plain img tags update correctly. The only workaround is renaming the file or deleting .next and restarting the dev server.
signals.review_reason: Breaks the dev loop for image iteration — developers cannot preview image changes without manual cache clearing. While not a production blocker, it significantly disrupts the most common daily workflow (dev iteration) for image-heavy pages.

source_issues.title: next/image in dev does not update local image after file edit with same filename
source_issues.evidence: next/image shows stale local image after editing the file without changing filename. Plain img tag updates correctly. Workaround requires renaming file or deleting .next cache and restarting dev server. Dev loop is broken for image iteration.

signals.topic: Metadata descriptions containing Windows carriage returns produce duplicate meta description tags on hydration
signals.summary: Metadata descriptions with Windows CR (\r\n) generate duplicate <meta name=description> tags. The CR is stripped in built HTML but retained in hydration data, causing Next to re-add the description during client hydration.
signals.review_reason: Produces invalid HTML (duplicate meta tags) that affects SEO and browser behavior. The issue silently corrupts the rendered page structure — a common Windows line-ending scenario causing real-world SEO impact.

source_issues.title: Metadata descriptions containing Windows carriage returns result in duplicate <meta> tags
source_issues.evidence: Windows carriage returns in metadata descriptions cause duplicate <meta name="description"> tags. The CR is stripped in built HTML but not in hydration data, so Next re-adds description during hydration. Results in two meta description tags on the client-rendered page.

signals.topic: Zod response validation error breaks `getProjects` after SDK upgrade
signals.summary: After upgrading SDK from 1.18.7 to 1.18.9, `getProjects` throws ZodError because the API returns `undefined` for fields like `alias` (expected array) and `security` (complex union schema with missing required nested fields), completely blocking project data retrieval.
aliases: SDK upgrade breaks getProjects with Zod schema mismatch
signals.review_reason: This is a real user-blocking issue: `getProjects` is a core SDK method and its failure after an SDK upgrade blocks the primary workflow of fetching project data. The ZodError indicates a schema drift between the API response and the SDK's type definitions, causing production failures. Count=1 (single repo, single issue) so P0 is not applicable per rules, but P1 is warranted given the main flow blocking nature. No exclusion criteria apply — this is not a security announcement, feature request, roadmap discussion, or maintenance item without user impact.

source_issues.title: `getProjects` response validation error
source_issues.evidence: User reports that after upgrading from SDK 1.18.7 to 1.18.9, `getProjects` throws massive ZodError: alias fields receive `undefined` instead of expected array, and the security field has complex union schema mismatches with missing required nested fields (vercel_ruleset, bot_filter, ai_bots, owasp). The issue has 5 comments, indicating others are affected.

signals.topic: Peer dependency incorrectly treated as workspace dependency causing unnecessary package builds
signals.summary: Turborepo's dependency graph incorrectly includes workspace packages as dependencies when a concrete npm dependency with the same name exists alongside a peer dependency pointing to a workspace package. This causes extra packages to be built unnecessarily, deviating from Yarn Berry's expected behavior.
aliases: peer deps treated as workspace deps
incorrect workspace inclusion from peer deps
signals.review_reason: Build graph incorrect: extra packages are built that should not be in the dependency graph. Causes wasted CI time and potential FFI/native module build failures. Two separate but thematically identical root causes (peer dep confusion + transparent workspaces not respected), both confirmed with reproduction repos. Both affect build correctness.

source_issues.title: Turborepo incorrectly viewing peer deps as workspace dependencies when concrete npm dependency exists
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction: workspace with concrete npm devDependency on 'buffer' package AND a peer dep pointing to workspace 'buffer'. Turbo builds extra workspaces (buffer, d, e) that Yarn Berry correctly excludes. Deviation from expected Yarn behaviour confirmed.

source_issues.title: Yarn 4: Respect `enableTransparentWorkspaces: false` when resolving workspace dependencies
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction: Yarn 4 workspace with npm: protocol dep same name as a local workspace. With enableTransparentWorkspaces=false, turbo incorrectly builds the local workspace package instead of using the npm dependency. FFI packages affected, CI builds broken.

signals.topic: pnpm 11 multi-document YAML lockfile causes workspace resolution failure and task abort
signals.summary: pnpm 11's configDependencies feature generates a multi-document YAML lockfile with a frontmatter section (pnpmfileChecksum). Turbo's lockfile parser cannot handle multi-document YAML, causing workspace resolution to fail and tasks to abort with 'Cannot find module' errors.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocked: workspace resolution fails entirely, task execution aborts with module-not-found errors. Clear reproduction path, turbo-specific regression confirmed. Count=1 but severity is high (task abort + workspace resolution failure).

source_issues.title: Turbo cannot parse pnpm 11 lockfiles with multi-document YAML (configDependencies)
source_issues.evidence: Warning 'Unable to convert to yaml: deserializing from YAML containing more than one document is not supported' → x Could not resolve workspaces → Error during pnpmfile execution 'Cannot find module' → Tasks abort. Reproduction: add configDependencies to pnpm-workspace.yaml, run turbo task, task fails. pnpm -r run typecheck (without turbo) works correctly, confirming turbo-specific regression.

signals.topic: Cache miss after deleting output files forces unnecessary rebuild
signals.summary: After a successful cached build, deleting output files in a sub-package (e.g., apps/nuxt/.output) causes Turbo to report a cache miss on the next build and trigger a full rebuild, instead of either restoring from cache or correctly detecting the cache as valid.
signals.review_reason: Significant build efficiency regression: users lose cache on output file deletion, forcing full rebuilds. Disrupts iterative dev workflows (e.g., deleting .next, .output, dist folders). Reproducible with clear step-by-step evidence.

source_issues.title: Cache miss after deleting output files
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction: first build hits cache (FULL TURBO), second build hits cache (FULL TURBO), delete apps/nuxt/.output directory, third build shows cache miss and rebuilds. Demonstrates clear CI/build loop regression where output deletion should not invalidate the global turbo cache.

signals.topic: Turborepo AI skill dispatcher generates incorrect guidance rejecting valid root tasks
signals.summary: The shipped /turborepo AI skill's slash-command dispatcher contains an absolute rule ('DO NOT create Root Tasks') that contradicts SKILL.md's nuanced guidance, causing AI agents to generate invalid Turborepo configurations that reject correct patterns like Vitest Projects' //#test.
aliases: turborepo skill dispatcher root task guidance error
AI skill root task rejection incorrect
signals.review_reason: AI-assisted tooling generates incorrect configuration guidance, leading to rejected valid Turborepo setups. While not a runtime crash, it blocks users relying on AI agents to configure their monorepo correctly. Real downstream PR impact confirmed.

source_issues.title: Turborepo skill: command dispatcher contradicts SKILL.md on Root Tasks
source_issues.evidence: command/turborepo.md line 44: 'DO NOT create Root Tasks' vs SKILL.md: 'Root Tasks are ONLY for tasks that truly cannot exist in packages (rare)'. AI agents following dispatcher generate incorrect guidance rejecting Vitest Projects //#test root task pattern, changeset tooling, and other valid root-level tasks. Downstream PR ValescoAgency/millsreg-sanity#67 demonstrates real usage impact.

signals.topic: CLI `vercel redeploy` fails authorization when VERCEL_ORG_ID is set, unlike other CLI commands that correctly honor org/project env vars
signals.summary: The `vercel redeploy` command does not call `getLinkedProject` to pull `VERCEL_ORG_ID` / `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` env vars, causing it to resolve team context from the wrong scope and produce a 'Not authorized' error. Other commands like `vercel list` work correctly with the same env vars.
aliases: CLI redeploy inconsistent with env vars
signals.review_reason: CLI redeploy flow is blocked (authorization error) when env vars are set. This is a clear main-flow failure: users in CI environments relying on VERCEL_ORG_ID for org-scoped deployments cannot use redeploy. The root cause is confirmed in code: redeploy bypasses getLinkedProject unlike other commands. P1 rather than P0 because count=1 and no additional confirming instances.

source_issues.title: Inconsistent cli flow between `list` and `redeploy` with env vars `VERCEL_ORG_ID`
source_issues.evidence: redeploy fails with 'Not authorized: Trying to access resource under scope ...' when using VERCEL_ORG_ID / VERCEL_TOKEN scoped to different teams; getScope resolves wrong team instead of honoring token scope

signals.topic: Next.js 16 post-build validation drops intermediate path segments from multi-segment Root Directory, causing ENOENT build failures in monorepos
signals.summary: When a Vercel project has a multi-segment Root Directory (e.g., `clients/admin-ui`) combined with a custom Build Command, Next.js 16 post-build validation computes file paths using only the basename, dropping the intermediate path segments. This causes ENOENT errors on files that exist at the correct location.
aliases: monorepo Root Directory ENOENT build failure
Next.js 16 multi-segment root path validation broken
signals.review_reason: Monorepo build is blocked at the post-build validation step with ENOENT errors. The deployment itself is complete but the validation fails, preventing successful deployment. Workaround requires complex symlink scripting during build. This is a primary CI/CD pipeline blocker for Next.js 16 monorepo users.

source_issues.title: Next.js 16 post-build validation drops intermediate path segments from multi-segment Root Directory
source_issues.evidence: Build fails with ENOENT after 'Build Completed' step; files exist at correct path /vercel/path0/clients/admin-ui/.next/... but validator looks at /vercel/path0/admin-ui/.next/... missing 'clients/' segment; workaround requires symlinking every subdirectory during build

signals.topic: CLI `vc link` links wrong project when project names share a common prefix, causing deployments to go to incorrect project
signals.summary: When two projects have names sharing a common prefix (e.g., `covillage` and `covillage-portal`), `vc link` correctly identifies the target project but writes the wrong OIDC token to .vercel/project.json, causing all subsequent deployments to route to the wrong project instead of `covillage-portal`.
aliases: vc link links wrong project prefix match
CLI link wrong OIDC token for similarly named projects
signals.review_reason: High severity: CLI link writes wrong OIDC token, causing all deployments to go to a different project. In a shared-namespace environment this could mean deploying to a competitor's project or a project with different configurations. This is a critical flow error: the user thinks they are linking project A but the system links project B. The wrong project gets updated while the correct project is left untouched.

source_issues.title: CLI: I can't deploy because `vc link` keeps linking wrong project
source_issues.evidence: Even when explicitly specifying --project prj_... or project name 'covillage-portal', .vercel/project.json gets OIDC token for 'covillage' instead; deployments go to wrong project; user can observe wrong project name in .vercel/project.json and env variable download shows wrong project name

signals.topic: CLI deployments (`vercel --prod`) no longer include Git commit metadata, breaking CI/CD traceability
signals.summary: Since approximately 2–3 days ago, deployments triggered via `vercel --prod` no longer attach Git commit metadata. The dashboard shows 'Source: vercel deploy' instead of the Git commit message, losing deployment-to-commit traceability.
aliases: CLI deploy missing Git commit reference
vercel --prod no longer shows commit message in dashboard
signals.review_reason: CLI deployments lose Git commit metadata, which is a core value proposition for Vercel's Git-based deployment workflow. Without commit metadata, teams lose the ability to trace which code was deployed, making rollback and audit trails unreliable. This is a clear regression affecting CI/CD pipelines. P1 because while deployments still succeed, the loss of metadata is significant for production workflows.

source_issues.title: CLI deploy (`vercel --prod`) no longer includes Git commit metadata
source_issues.evidence: Dashboard shows 'Source: vercel deploy' instead of commit message; git log confirms correct repo state; regression within last 2-3 days; no changes made to user workflow; deployments still succeed but lose critical audit trail

signals.topic: Vercel Toolbar iframe fails to load under COEP=credentialless due to missing Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy header on vercel.live
signals.summary: When a customer app sets Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy (COEP) to credentialless or require-corp, the Vercel Toolbar iframe from vercel.live is blocked because the response lacks a Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy header. The browser assigns chrome-error:// as the iframe origin, breaking the toolbar's postMessage handshake.
aliases: toolbar fails under cross-origin isolation policy
signals.review_reason: Vercel Toolbar is a core developer feature for preview deployments. When COEP is set (which is the recommended posture per Chrome's Spectre mitigation guidance), the toolbar fails to render entirely. This forces developers to choose between security isolation and using Vercel's development tools. The workaround of dropping COEP reduces app security posture.

source_issues.title: @vercel/toolbar iframe from vercel.live missing CORP header, fails to embed under COEP=credentialless
source_issues.evidence: Browser console shows 'Unsafe attempt to load URL https://vercel.live/_next-live/feedback/feedback.html from frame with URL chrome-error://chromewebdata'; COEP isolation prevents toolbar mount on preview deployments; workaround requires dropping COEP to 'unsafe-none' reducing app isolation guarantees

signals.topic: Zed crashes on git worktree creation failure (deleted worktree recreated)
signals.summary: When a user creates a worktree from a previously-deleted worktree, Zed panics and crashes with a full core dump instead of handling the error gracefully. The crash is triggered by an assertion failure in the Rust panic handler, indicating an unrecoverable state that should have been handled gracefully.
signals.review_reason: This is a reproducible crash that terminates the editor with a panic/assertion failure. While count=1, the crash is well-documented with a full stack trace and clear reproduction steps. The worktree workflow is a legitimate main-path feature, and an unhandled panic on a recoverable error (deleted worktree) represents a significant user impact: unsaved work risk and complete session loss.

source_issues.title: Zed crashes when git worktree creation fails
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction: create thread+worktree -> delete worktree -> reopen thread (selects non-existent worktree) -> select 'Create new worktree based on HEAD' -> Zed crashes with full core dump (Thread 0 Crashed). Crash occurs in std::panicking::panic_handler, indicating an unhandled assertion failure that should have been caught.

signals.topic: Git branch picker and worktree creation completely non-functional on WSL2 remote projects
signals.summary: When opening a project via Zed's remote projects feature in WSL2, the git branch picker shows zero branches and worktree creation fails. Root cause suspected to be incorrect path handling (backslash usage on Linux path).
signals.review_reason: Two core git workflow features (branch picker + worktree creator) are completely broken for WSL2 users, who represent a significant portion of Zed's Windows user base. The issue is labeled priority:P1 by triage and is reproducible. This blocks critical development workflow features for the affected platform.

source_issues.title: Git worktree creator and branch picker don't work on WSL2
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction on WSL2 with Zed remote projects: branch picker shows no branches at all; worktree creation fails with backslash path error. Labeled priority:P1, reproducible. Native Windows file system projects work fine, confirming WSL2-specific path handling bug.

signals.topic: Claude Opus 4.7 on AWS Bedrock fails all inference due to incorrect model ID suffix
signals.summary: The Bedrock model ID for Claude Opus 4.7 is defined as 'anthropic.claude-opus-4-7-v1' in Zed's code, but AWS's published ID is 'anthropic.claude-opus-4-7' (no '-v1' suffix). This causes all inference-profile routing to fail with 'Claude Opus 4.7 is not available in <region>' regardless of region or account authorization.
signals.review_reason: The core AI agent feature is completely non-functional for all Bedrock users using Claude Opus 4.7. The bug is labeled frequency:always and priority:P1, with precise technical evidence from AWS API responses. This is not a cosmetic issue — users pay for Bedrock access and cannot use the primary agent model. The root cause is a single-character string suffix mismatch.

source_issues.title: Claude Opus 4.7 on Bedrock model ID has incorrect "-v1" suffix, breaking inference profile routing
source_issues.evidence: Labeled frequency:always and priority:P1 by Zed triage. Confirmed with AWS API that the account is authorized for the correct model ID. Constructed request uses 'global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7-v1' which does not exist on Bedrock. Tested across us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-2, eu-west-1 — all fail identically. Claude Sonnet 4.6 has same suspected pattern.

signals.topic: Zed Pro edit_file tool silently fails when Claude Opus/Sonnet models attempt code edits

signals.review_reason: This blocks the core value proposition of a paid feature (Zed Pro AI coding). The edit_file tool failure is described as 'constantly' occurring, which indicates a systematic issue rather than a one-off. However, triage state is still 'needs info', so there's some uncertainty about root cause. Lower confidence but high user impact justifies P1 with keep=true.

source_issues.title: edit_file tool keep failing on v0.232.3
source_issues.evidence: User reports all file edit operations fail 'constantly' when using Zed Pro with Claude Opus or Sonnet in write mode. 4 comments indicate ongoing discussion. Error visible in UI screenshot. Users paying for Zed Pro cannot perform the core AI coding task.

signals.topic: Zed startup shows 'Failed to load database file' error popup with silent fallback to in-memory DB
signals.summary: On startup, Zed shows an error popup 'Failed to load database file' but provides no actionable guidance. The application falls back to an in-memory database, meaning all state (workspaces, settings, sessions) is lost across restarts.
signals.review_reason: Database migration failure on startup results in silent data loss (workspace state falls back to in-memory). While not a hard crash, losing all workspace state on every restart is a significant experience degradation for affected users. Count=1 prevents P1. Marked P2 because the editor still starts and works, just without persistent state.

source_issues.title: "Failed to load database file" popup
source_issues.evidence: Log shows 'Migration changed for WorkspaceDb at step 36' — schema migration conflict between stored and proposed migration. Application falls back to in-memory database (WARN [db] Opening fallback in-memory database). This means workspace state is lost on every restart. Popup provides no resolution path.
